questions.q: Choose the correct passive voice of: "She writes a letter."
o: A letter is written by her.
She is written by a letter.

A letter has been written by her.
questions.e: Simple present active becomes simple present passive: is + past participle.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct passive voice of: "He repaired the car."
o: The car has been repaired by him.
He was repaired by the car.
The car was repaired by him.
The car is repaired by him.
questions.e: Simple past active becomes simple past passive: was + past participle.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct passive voice of: "They will build a bridge."
o: A bridge will be built by them.
A bridge is built by them.

A bridge would be built by them.
questions.e: Future active becomes 'will be + past participle' in the passive.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct passive voice of: "The teacher praised the students."
o: The students have been praised by the teacher.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct passive voice of: "She is cooking food."

questions.e: Present continuous active becomes 'is being + past participle' in the passive.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct passive voice of: "He has finished the work."
o: He has been finished by the work.
The work was finished by him.
The work is finished by him.
The work has been finished by him.
questions.e: Present perfect active becomes 'has been + past participle' in the passive.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct passive voice of: "Open the door."
questions.e: Imperative sentences become 'Let + object + be + past participle'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct passive voice of: "Who broke the window?"

o: He said that he is tired.

questions.subject: English

o: She told that she would come tomorrow.

questions.subject: English

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech of: She said, "Please help me."
o: She requested me to help her.

o: He said that he has finished his work.

He told that he had finished his work.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is 12% of 800?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: In a class of 60 students, 45% are girls. How many boys are in the class?
questions.e: Boys make up 100 - 45 = 55% of the class, and 55% of 60 = 33.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A shopkeeper offers a 20% discount on a watch priced at Rs. 2,500. What is the selling price?
questions.e: Discount = 20% of 2,500 = Rs. 500, so the selling price = 2,500 - 500 = Rs. 2,000.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A price is first increased by 10% and then decreased by 10%. What is the net percentage change?
questions.e: For a 10% rise followed by a 10% fall, the net change is always a decrease of (10 x 10)/100 = 1%. The loss comes from applying the fall to the already-increased price.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A shop's monthly rent was Rs. 8,000. After a 25% hike, by what percentage must it now be reduced to return to Rs. 8,000?
questions.e: After a 25% rise the rent is Rs. 10,000; the Rs. 2,000 cut is 2,000/10,000 x 100 = 20% of the raised rent.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A candidate's vote share fell from 45% to 36% between two elections. What was the percentage decrease in his vote share?
questions.e: The drop of 45 - 36 = 9 percentage points on a base of 45 gives (9/45) x 100 = 20%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Kavita's income is 50% more than Neha's. By what percentage is Neha's income less than Kavita's?
questions.e: If Kavita earns 50% more, take Neha's income as 100 and Kavita's as 150. The difference 50 is 33.33% of 150, so Neha earns 33.33% less.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Kavita's income is 25% more than Amit's. By what percentage is Amit's income less than Kavita's?
questions.e: If Kavita earns 25% more, take Amit's income as 100 and Kavita's as 125. The difference 25 is 20% of 125, so Amit earns 20% less.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A shopkeeper offers two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on the marked price of a shirt. What is the equivalent single discount?
questions.e: After the 20% discount the price is 80% of the marked price; the 10% discount then applies to that, giving 80% × 90% = 72% of the marked price. So the total reduction is 28%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Divide Rs. 500 between A and B in the ratio 2:3. How much does A receive?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Two friends start a business investing Rs. 12,000 and Rs. 18,000. If the year-end profit is Rs. 9,000, what is the larger partner's share?
questions.e: Investments are in the ratio 12,000:18,000 = 2:3, so the larger share = 9,000 x 3/5 = Rs. 5,400.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The ages of a father and his son are in the ratio 7:3. If the sum of their ages is 60 years, how old is the father?
questions.e: Father's age = 60 x 7/(7+3) = 42 years.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The ratio of the ages of Priya and Amit is 2:3. If the sum of their ages is 40 years, how old is Priya?
questions.e: Priya's age = 40 x 2/(2+3) = 16 years.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The ratio of the ages of Neha and Pooja is 3:4. If the sum of their ages is 42 years, how old is Neha?
questions.e: Neha's age = 42 x 3/(3+4) = 18 years.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The ratio of the ages of Ravi and Sita is 3:4. If the sum of their ages is 63 years, how old is Ravi?
questions.e: Ravi's age = 63 x 3/(3+4) = 27 years.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the fourth proportional to 5, 15 and 6.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: On a map, 3 cm represents 12 km of actual distance. What actual distance does 7 cm represent?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A printer prints 45 pages in 3 minutes. How many pages can it print in 11 minutes at the same rate?
questions.e: Pages and minutes are in direct proportion: x = (45 x 11)/3 = 165 pages.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the mean proportional between 25 and 36.
questions.e: The mean proportional is the square root of the product: sqrt(25 x 36) = 30.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If m is the mean proportional between 8 and 18, what is the value of m^2?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The mean proportional between 12 and 27 is added to the fourth proportional to 4, 6 and 9. What is the total?
questions.e: Mean proportional = sqrt(12 x 27) = 18; fourth proportional x = (6 x 9)/4 = 13.5; total = 18 + 13.5 = 31.5.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the average of the first 60 natural numbers.
questions.e: The average of the first 60 natural numbers is (n+1)/2 = 61/2 = 30.5.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A batsman scores 45, 32, 78, 56 and 89 in five innings. What is his average score per innings?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The ages of five team members are 24, 28, 31, 26 and 36 years. What is the average age of the team?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The average age of 12 persons is 35 years. If one person aged 60 years is replaced by a new person, the average rises to 38 years. Find the age of the new person.
questions.e: Total age rises by 12 x (38 - 35) = 36 years, so the new person's age is 60 + 36 = 96 years.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The average monthly salary of 20 employees is Rs. 45,000. A new manager joins and the average rises to Rs. 47,000. What is the manager's salary?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: In a class of 30 students the average weight is 48 kg. When the teacher's weight is included, the average becomes 49 kg. What is the teacher's weight?
questions.e: New total = 31 x 49 = 1,519 kg; old total = 30 x 48 = 1,440 kg; teacher = 1,519 - 1,440 = 79 kg.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A student scores a total of 300 marks in 6 subjects. What is his average score per subject?
questions.e: Average = total marks / number of subjects = 300/6 = 50.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A bowler takes 2, 3, 1, 4 and 0 wickets in five matches. What is his average wickets per match?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the simple interest on Rs. 10000 at 6% per annum for 3 years.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Ravi lends Rs. 12,000 to a friend. After 4 years he receives Rs. 16,800 in total. What annual rate of simple interest did he charge?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What sum of money will yield Rs. 2,400 as simple interest over 6 years at 10% per annum?
questions.e: Principal = (100 x interest)/(rate x time) = (100 x 2,400)/(10 x 6) = Rs. 4,000.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: At what rate percent per annum will Rs. 2000 double itself in 25 years at simple interest?
questions.e: Interest needed equals the principal (Rs. 2000). Rate = (100 x interest)/(P x T) = 100/25 = 4% per annum.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times the original sum?
questions.e: Doubling in 8 years fixes the rate; earning three times the principal as interest takes 3 x 8 = 24 years.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Meena deposits Rs. 25,000 in a scheme paying 12% simple interest per annum. How much interest will she earn in 9 months?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the compound interest on Rs. 4000 at 8% per annum for 2 years.
questions.e: Amount after 2 years = 4000 x (1 + 8/100)^2 = Rs. 4665.6, so CI = amount - principal = Rs. 665.6.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Rs. 10,000 is invested at 10% per annum compounded annually. What is the amount after 3 years?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The population of a town is 80,000 and grows at 5% per annum compounded yearly. What will the population be after 2 years?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on Rs. 10000 at 20% per annum for 2 years is:

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: On a certain sum, the simple interest for 2 years at 10% per annum is Rs. 400. What is the compound interest on the same sum at the same rate for the same period?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A sum lent at 15% per annum compound interest amounts to Rs. 13,225 in 2 years. What was the original sum?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs. 400 and sells it for Rs. 460. Find the profit percentage.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A fruit vendor buys 2 dozen bananas for Rs. 120 and sells each banana at Rs. 7. What is his profit percentage?
questions.e: Cost per banana = 120/24 = Rs. 5; profit = Rs. 2; profit% = (2/5) x 100 = 40%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: By selling a watch for Rs. 1,440, a dealer makes a profit equal to one-fifth of its cost price. What is the cost price?
questions.e: Selling price = cost + cost/5 = 6 x cost/5, so cost = 1,440 x 5/6 = Rs. 1,200.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: An article bought for Rs. 800 is sold at a profit of 10%. Find the selling price.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A trader marks a toy 30% above its cost price of Rs. 500 and sells it with no discount. What is the selling price?
questions.e: Selling price = 500 x 130/100 = Rs. 650.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A bookseller buys 50 notebooks for Rs. 2,000 and wants a 25% profit overall. At what price per notebook must he sell?
questions.e: Total selling price = 2,000 x 125/100 = Rs. 2,500; per notebook = 2,500/50 = Rs. 50.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: An article is sold for Rs. 720 at a loss of 10%. Find its cost price.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A cycle sold at a 20% loss fetches Rs. 3,200. If it had been sold at a 20% profit instead, what would the selling price have been?
questions.e: Cost = 3,200 x 100/80 = Rs. 4,000; selling price at 20% profit = 4,000 x 120/100 = Rs. 4,800.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A dishonest dealer claims to sell at cost price but uses a 900 g weight instead of 1 kg. What is his profit percentage?
questions.e: He sells 900 g for the price of 1,000 g, so profit = (100/900) x 100 = 11.11%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A man sells two articles at Rs. 1500 each. On one he gains 25% and on the other he loses 25%. What is his overall profit or loss%?
questions.e: When SP is the same and gain% equals loss%, there is always a loss of (x^2/100)% = (25^2/100)% = 6.25%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A shopkeeper sells a shirt at a 10% profit and a pair of shoes at a 10% loss, each for Rs. 990. What is the net result?
questions.e: Costs are 990/1.1 = Rs. 900 and 990/0.9 = Rs. 1,100 (total Rs. 2,000); total selling price Rs. 1,980, a loss of Rs. 20 = 1%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A dealer sells two tables for Rs. 9,000 each - one at a 50% profit and the other at a 25% loss. What is his overall result?
questions.e: Costs are 9,000/1.5 = Rs. 6,000 and 9,000/0.75 = Rs. 12,000 (total Rs. 18,000); total selling price is also Rs. 18,000, so no profit, no loss.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The marked price of an article is Rs. 1500. It is sold at a discount of 25%. Find the selling price.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: During a sale, a jacket with a price tag of Rs. 2,400 is offered at one-fourth off. What does the customer pay?
questions.e: One-fourth off means the customer pays three-fourths: 2,400 x 3/4 = Rs. 1,800.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A shopkeeper allows a 12% discount on a mixer priced at Rs. 3,500. What is the discount amount in rupees?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the single equivalent discount for two successive discounts of 25% and 25%.
questions.e: Equivalent discount = d1 + d2 - (d1 x d2)/100 = 25 + 25 - 6.25 = 43.75%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What single discount is equivalent to a 50% discount followed by a 20% discount?
questions.e: Equivalent discount = 50 + 20 - (50 x 20)/100 = 60%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A shop offers 20% off on all shoes, plus an extra 10% off the reduced price at billing. What overall discount does a customer get?
questions.e: Overall discount = 20 + 10 - (20 x 10)/100 = 28%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Pooja can complete a task in 20 days and Priya in 30 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.e: Together they do (1/20 + 1/30) of the work per day = 50/600, so time taken = 600/50 = 12 days.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Ravi can complete a task in 8 days and Neha in 24 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.e: Together they do (1/8 + 1/24) of the work per day = 32/192, so time taken = 192/32 = 6 days.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Vikash can complete a task in 5 days and Sita in 15 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.e: Together they do (1/5 + 1/15) of the work per day = 20/75, so time taken = 75/20 = 3.75 days.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: 12 men can do a piece of work in 10 days. In how many days can 10 men do the same work?
questions.e: Total work = 12 x 10 = 120 man-days, so 10 men take 120/10 = 12 days.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A can finish a job in 12 days and B can finish the same job in 15 days. How long will they take working together?
questions.e: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/15 = 9/60 per day, so time = 60/9 = 20/3 days = 6 days 16 hours.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours while pipe B can empty it in 8 hours. If both pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the empty tank?
questions.e: Net filling rate = 1/6 - 1/8 = 1/24 per hour, so the tank fills in 24 hours.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Neha and Pooja do a piece of work in the ratio 2:3 and earn Rs. 600 together. What is Neha's share?
questions.e: Wages are shared in the ratio of work done: Neha gets 600 x 2/5 = Rs. 240.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Suresh and Neha do a piece of work in the ratio 4:5 and earn Rs. 900 together. What is Suresh's share?
questions.e: Wages are shared in the ratio of work done: Suresh gets 900 x 4/9 = Rs. 400.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Pooja and Vikash do a piece of work in the ratio 2:3 and earn Rs. 500 together. What is Pooja's share?
questions.e: Wages are shared in the ratio of work done: Pooja gets 500 x 2/5 = Rs. 200.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A car travels at 50 km/h for 4 hours. What distance does it cover?
questions.e: Distance = speed x time = 50 x 4 = 200 km.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A train running at a steady 90 km/h leaves Delhi at 6 AM. How far has it travelled by 10 AM?
questions.e: Time elapsed = 4 hours; distance = 90 x 4 = 360 km.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A cyclist rides 3 hours in the morning at 18 km/h and 2 hours in the evening at 15 km/h. What total distance does he cover in the day?
questions.e: Distance = 18 x 3 + 15 x 2 = 54 + 30 = 84 km.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A man travels from town A to town B at 40 km/h and returns by the same route at 60 km/h. Find his average speed for the whole journey.
questions.e: Average speed for equal distances = 2xy/(x+y) = (2 x 40 x 60)/(40+60) = 48 km/h. It is the harmonic mean, not the simple average.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Priya drives to the market at 30 km/h and returns home along the same road at 20 km/h. What is her average speed for the round trip?
questions.e: For equal distances, average speed = 2xy/(x+y) = (2 x 30 x 20)/50 = 24 km/h.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A bus covers the first half of a 240 km route at 60 km/h and the second half at 40 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole route?
questions.e: The halves are equal, so average speed = (2 x 60 x 40)/(60+40) = 48 km/h.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A 270 m long train running at 54 km/h crosses a pole in how many seconds?
questions.e: Speed = 54 x 5/18 = 15 m/s. Time = distance/speed = 270/15 = 18 seconds.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A 150 m long metro train crosses a signal post in 10 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: An express train running at 90 km/h crosses a telegraph pole in 12 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.e: 90 km/h = 25 m/s; length = speed x time = 25 x 12 = 300 m.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A 180 m long train running at 72 km/h crosses a 220 m long platform in how many seconds?
questions.e: Total distance = 180 + 220 = 400 m; speed = 72 x 5/18 = 20 m/s; time = 400/20 = 20 seconds.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A 250 m long goods train running at 36 km/h crosses a 350 m long bridge. How many seconds does it take?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A 120 m long local train crosses a 180 m platform in 20 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A boat's speed in still water is 8 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. How long will it take to travel 30 km upstream?
questions.e: Upstream speed = 8 - 3 = 5 km/h, so time = 30/5 = 6 hours.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A swimmer's speed in still water is 5 km/h and the river flows at 2 km/h. How long will he take to swim 21 km downstream?
questions.e: Downstream speed = 5 + 2 = 7 km/h; time = 21/7 = 3 hours.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A boat travels 36 km downstream in 4 hours and the stream's speed is 2 km/h. What is the boat's speed in still water?
questions.e: Downstream speed = 36/4 = 9 km/h; still-water speed = 9 - 2 = 7 km/h.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: In what ratio must two varieties of rice costing Rs. 40 and Rs. 70 per kg be mixed so that the mixture costs Rs. 50 per kg?
questions.e: By alligation: (cheaper variety):(dearer variety) = (70-50):(50-40) = 2:1.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A milkman mixes water with milk costing Rs. 60 per litre and sells the mixture at Rs. 50 per litre, making no profit and no loss. How much water does he add per litre of milk?
questions.e: By alligation, milk:water = (50-0):(60-50) = 5:1, so per litre of milk he adds 1/5 litre = 200 ml of water.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A student must score 30% to pass an exam. He scores 210 marks and fails by 60 marks. Find the maximum marks.
questions.e: Pass marks = 210 + 60 = 270, which is 30% of the maximum. Maximum = 270 x 100/30 = 900.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: In a village election, the winning candidate got 55% of the votes and won by 600 votes. How many votes were cast in total?
questions.e: Winner 55% and runner-up 45% differ by 10% = 600 votes, so total votes = 600 x 100/10 = 6,000.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A fruit seller sold 40% of his oranges in the morning and 30% of the remainder in the evening, leaving 210 oranges. How many did he start with?
questions.e: Left = 70% of 60% = 42% of the stock = 210, so stock = 210 x 100/42 = 500 oranges.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the unit digit of 3^84.
questions.e: Only the unit digit of the base matters. The powers of 3 repeat their unit digits in a cycle of 4, and 84 mod 4 = 0, giving a unit digit of 1.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is the unit digit of 7^4 x 3^3?
questions.e: 7^4 = 2401 ends in 1 and 3^3 = 27 ends in 7, so the product ends in 1 x 7 = 7.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is the unit digit of 13^5 + 17^6?
questions.e: 13^5 ends in 3 (cycle of 3 is 3,9,7,1) and 17^6 ends in 9 (cycle of 7 is 7,9,3,1); 3 + 9 = 12, so the sum ends in 2.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 3?
questions.e: Test each option: 4215 is divisible by 3 because sum of digits divisible by 3.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The number 4*37 is divisible by 11. What digit should replace the star?
questions.e: For divisibility by 11, (7+4) - (3+star) must be 0, so star = 8.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is the smallest 4-digit number divisible by 12?
questions.e: 1000 divided by 12 leaves remainder 4, so add 8: 1008 = 84 x 12.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the LCM of 8 and 10.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the HCF of 24 and 48.
questions.e: List the factors: the greatest common factor of 24 and 48 is 24.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Three bells toll together and then at intervals of 12, 18 and 20 minutes respectively. After how many minutes will they toll together again?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Simplify: 12 + 6 x 4 - 24 / 6
questions.e: By BODMAS, do multiplication and division first: 12 + 24 - 4 = 32.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.e: Brackets first: (6 + 2) = 8; then division and multiplication left to right: 48 / 8 = 6, 6 x 5 = 30; then 3^2 = 9; 30 - 9 = 21.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Simplify: 2/3 + 2/5
questions.e: Take the common denominator 15: (10 + 6)/15 = 16/15.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Ravi spends 1/3 of his pocket money on books and 1/4 on snacks. What fraction of his pocket money does he spend in total?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is the square root of 1024?
questions.e: Since 32 x 32 = 1024, the square root of 1024 is 32.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A square garden has an area of 2,025 sq m. What is the length of one side of the garden?
questions.e: Side = sqrt(2025) = 45 m, since 45 x 45 = 2025.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the cube root of 512.
questions.e: Since 8^3 = 512, the cube root of 512 is 8.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The volume of a cubic box is 3,375 cubic cm. What is the length of its edge?
questions.e: Edge = cube root of 3375 = 15 cm, since 15^3 = 3375.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If x + 1/x = 6, find the value of x^2 + 1/x^2.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The quadratic equation x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0 has which of the following as its roots?
questions.e: x^2 - 7x + 12 = (x-3)(x-4), so the roots are 3 and 4.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If p + q = 8 and p - q = 2, what is the value of pq?
questions.e: Solving gives p = 5 and q = 3, so pq = 15.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If a + b = 7 and ab = 12, find the value of a^2 + b^2.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The sum of two numbers is 15 and their difference is 3. What is the product of the numbers?
questions.e: The numbers are (15+3)/2 = 9 and (15-3)/2 = 6; product = 54.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: For the equation m^2 - 5m + 6 = 0, what is the sum of its roots?
questions.e: By the sum-of-roots rule, sum = -(-5) = 5.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the area of a square of side 20 cm.
questions.e: Area of a square = side^2 = 20^2 = 400 sq cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the perimeter of a square of side 12 cm.
questions.e: Perimeter of a square = 4 x side = 4 x 12 = 48 cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The length of a rectangle is 25 m and its breadth is 10 m. Find its area.
questions.e: Area = length x breadth = 25 x 10 = 250 sq m.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A rectangular plot 40 m long has a perimeter of 110 m. What is its area?
questions.e: Breadth = 110/2 - 40 = 15 m; area = 40 x 15 = 600 sq m.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the area of a circle of radius 21 cm. (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.e: Area = pi x r^2 = (22/7) x 21 x 21 = 1386 sq cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A circular garden has a diameter of 28 m. What is the cost of fencing it at Rs. 15 per metre? (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.e: Fence length = pi x d = (22/7) x 28 = 88 m; cost = 88 x 15 = Rs. 1,320.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The area of a circular park is 154 sq m. What is its radius? (Use pi = 22/7)

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the area of a triangle with base 16 cm and height 6 cm.
questions.e: Area = (1/2) x base x height = (1/2) x 16 x 6 = 48 sq cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The base of a triangle is twice its height, and its area is 81 sq cm. What is the base?
questions.e: (1/2) x 2h x h = h^2 = 81, so h = 9 cm and base = 18 cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the total surface area of a cube of side 5 cm.
questions.e: Total surface area = 6 x side^2 = 6 x 5^2 = 150 sq cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the volume of a cube of side 4 cm.
questions.e: Volume of a cube = side^3 = 4^3 = 64 cubic cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the volume of a cuboid of length 10 cm, breadth 6 cm and height 5 cm.
questions.e: Volume = l x b x h = 10 x 6 x 5 = 300 cubic cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A water tank is 2 m long, 1.5 m wide and 1 m deep. How many litres of water does it hold when full?
questions.e: Volume = 2 x 1.5 x 1 = 3 cubic m = 3,000 litres.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 30 cm. (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.e: Volume = pi x r^2 x h = (22/7) x 7^2 x 30 = 4620 cubic cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A cylindrical oil drum has a diameter of 1.4 m and holds 3.08 cubic m of oil. What is its height? (Use pi = 22/7)

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the surface area of a sphere of radius 14 cm. (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.e: Surface area = 4 x pi x r^2 = 4 x (22/7) x 14^2 = 2464 sq cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A hemispherical bowl of radius 7 cm is to be painted inside and outside. What total area is painted? (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.e: Two curved surfaces of 2 x pi x r^2 each = 4 x pi x r^2 = 4 x (22/7) x 49 = 616 sq cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the volume of a cone of radius 14 cm and height 30 cm. (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.e: Volume = (1/3) x pi x r^2 x h = (1/3) x (22/7) x 14^2 x 30 = 6160 cubic cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: An ice-cream cone of radius 3.5 cm and height 12 cm is completely full of ice cream. What is the volume of the ice cream? (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.e: Volume = (1/3) x pi x r^2 x h = (1/3) x (22/7) x 3.5 x 3.5 x 12 = 154 cubic cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Two complementary angles are in the ratio 1:4. Find the larger angle.
questions.e: Complementary angles sum to 90 degrees, so the larger is 90 x 4/(1+4) = 72 degrees.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Two supplementary angles are in the ratio 2:3. Find the smaller angle.
questions.e: Supplementary angles sum to 180 degrees, so the smaller = 180 x 2/5 = 72 degrees.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The difference between two complementary angles is 20 degrees. Find the larger angle.
questions.e: Larger angle = (90 + 20)/2 = 55 degrees.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 3:4:5. Find the largest angle.
questions.e: The angles sum to 180 degrees, so the largest is 180 x 5/12 = 75 degrees.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: In triangle ABC, angle A is twice angle B and angle C is thrice angle B. What is the measure of angle A?
questions.e: 2B + B + 3B = 180 degrees, so B = 30 degrees and A = 60 degrees.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm. (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.e: Circumference = 2 x pi x r = 2 x (22/7) x 7 = 44 cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A wheel makes 500 revolutions in covering 1.1 km. What is the diameter of the wheel? (Use pi = 22/7)
questions.e: One revolution = 1,100/500 = 2.2 m; diameter = 2.2 x 7/22 = 0.7 m = 70 cm.

questions.subject: Quant

questions.e: From the standard trigonometric table, sin 60° = √3/2.

questions.subject: Quant

questions.e: From the standard trigonometric table, cos 90° = 0.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If sin A = 3/5 and A is an acute angle, what is the value of cos A?
questions.e: cos A = sqrt(1 - sin^2 A) = sqrt(1 - 9/25) = sqrt(16/25) = 4/5.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is the value of tan 0°?
questions.e: From the standard trigonometric table, tan 0° = 0.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If tan θ = 5/12, find the value of sin θ. (θ is acute)
questions.e: Take opposite = 5 and adjacent = 12; hypotenuse = 13 (a 5-12-13 triangle). Then sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 5/13.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If cos theta = 8/17 and theta is acute, find the value of tan theta.
questions.e: From the 8-15-17 triangle, sin theta = 15/17, so tan theta = sin/cos = 15/8.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Which number comes next in the series of perfect cubes 1, 8, 27, 64, ...?
questions.e: These are the cubes 1^3, 2^3, 3^3, 4^3, so the next term is 5^3 = 125.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Find the next number in the doubling series 3, 6, 12, 24, ...
questions.e: Each term is multiplied by 2, so the next term is 24 x 2 = 48.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is the next term of the Fibonacci-like series 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ...?
questions.e: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 8 = 3 + 5, 13 = 5 + 8, 21 = 8 + 13, so the next is 13 + 21 = 34.

questions.subject: Quant

questions.subject: Quant

questions.q: The first row of a stadium has 25 seats, and each row after it has 8 more seats than the row before. How many seats are in the 6th row?
questions.e: The rows form an AP: 25, 33, ...; the 6th term = 25 + (6 - 1) x 8 = 65.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Rita saves Rs. 500 in January and increases her savings by Rs. 150 every month. How much does she save in June?
questions.e: Monthly savings form an AP with first term 500 and difference 150; June is the 6th term: 500 + 5 x 150 = Rs. 1,250.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: The 3rd term of an arithmetic progression is 17 and the 7th term is 33. What is the first term?
questions.e: Common difference = (33 - 17)/(7 - 3) = 4; first term = 17 - 2 x 4 = 9.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: What is the 20th term of the arithmetic progression 7, 12, 17, ...?

questions.subject: Reasoning
