questions.e: Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata are Indian cities, while Paris is in France.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the odd one out: Triangle, Square, Rectangle, Circle
questions.e: Triangle, square and rectangle are made of straight lines, while a circle has no straight side.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the odd one out: Copper, Iron, Gold, Wood
questions.e: Copper, iron and gold are metals, while wood is not a metal.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the odd one out: Rose, Lotus, Marigold, Mango
questions.e: Rose, lotus and marigold are flowers, while mango is a fruit.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the odd one out: January, March, May, June
questions.e: January, March and May have 31 days, while June has 30 days.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the odd one out: Dog, Cat, Lion, Table
questions.e: Dog, cat and lion are animals, while a table is furniture.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi said, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the woman related to Ravi?
questions.e: The grandfather's only son is Ravi's father, and the father's daughter is Ravi's sister.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A is B's brother. B is C's mother. How is A related to C?
questions.e: A is the brother of C's mother, which makes A the maternal uncle of C.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Pointing to a man, Sita said, 'He is the brother of my mother's husband.' How is the man related to Sita?
questions.e: Sita's mother's husband is her father, and her father's brother is her uncle.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: X is the father of Y, and Y is the sister of Z. How is X related to Z?
questions.e: X is the father of Y, and since Y and Z are siblings, X is also the father of Z.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: P is Q's sister. Q is R's brother. R is S's mother. How is P related to S?
questions.e: P, Q and R are siblings, and R is S's mother, so P is S's aunt.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Rahul's mother is the only daughter of Seema's father. How is Seema related to Rahul?
questions.e: The only daughter of Seema's father is Seema herself, so Seema is Rahul's mother.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: How is the son of your father's sister related to you?
questions.e: Your father's sister is your aunt, and her son is your cousin.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Anita's mother is the only daughter of Sunita's father. How is Sunita related to Anita?
questions.e: Sunita's father has only one daughter, and that daughter is Sunita herself. Since she is Anita's mother, Sunita is Anita's mother.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A girl's brother's father's wife is related to the girl as her ___?
questions.e: The brother's father is also the girl's father, and his wife is her mother.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If P + Q means P is the father of Q and P - Q means P is the wife of Q, what does A + B - C mean?
o: A is the brother of C
A is the father of C
A is the father-in-law of C
A is the son of C
questions.e: A is the father of B, and B is the wife of C, so A is the father of C's wife, i.e. C's father-in-law.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A man walks 5 km towards the north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns left and walks 2 km. In which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.e: He ends 3 km east and 7 km north of the start, which is the north-east direction.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Ravi faces east, turns 90 degrees clockwise, then turns 180 degrees anticlockwise. Which direction does he face now?
questions.e: East turned 90 degrees clockwise is south; turning 180 degrees anticlockwise from south gives north.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A person walks 4 km south, turns left and walks 6 km, then turns right and walks 4 km. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.e: He is 6 km east and 8 km south of the start; distance = sqrt(36+64) = 10 km.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: If north becomes east, north-east becomes ___?
questions.e: The whole compass rotates 90 degrees clockwise, so north-east rotates to south-east.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A man walks 3 km east and then 4 km north. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.e: The path forms a 3-4-5 right triangle, so the straight-line distance is 5 km.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Sita walks 2 km west, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 2 km. In which direction is she from the starting point?
questions.e: She ends at the same east-west line as the start but 3 km to the south.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A cyclist rides 10 km north, then 10 km east, then 10 km south. How far is he from the starting point?
questions.e: The north and south legs cancel out, leaving him 10 km east of the start.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A watch shows 3:00. If the hour hand points north, in which direction does the minute hand point?
questions.e: At 3:00 the minute hand is at 12, which is 90 degrees clockwise from the hour hand at 3; if 3 points north, 12 points east.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All pens are books. All books are chairs. Conclusions: I. All pens are chairs. II. Some chairs are pens. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: Pens are inside books which are inside chairs, so all pens are chairs and some chairs are pens.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: Some cats are dogs. All dogs are animals. Conclusions: I. Some cats are animals. II. All cats are animals. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: The cats that are dogs must be animals, but nothing is said about all cats.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: No bird is a fish. All fish are swimmers. Conclusions: I. No bird is a swimmer. II. Some swimmers are fish. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: All fish are swimmers, so some swimmers are definitely fish; birds may or may not swim.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All A are B. Some B are C. Conclusions: I. Some A are C. II. All C are A. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: The B's that are C need not overlap with the B's that are A.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: Some mangoes are fruits. All fruits are sweet. Conclusions: I. Some mangoes are sweet. II. All mangoes are sweet. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: The mangoes that are fruits are sweet, but not necessarily all mangoes.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All students are hardworking. No hardworking person is lazy. Conclusions: I. No student is lazy. II. Some lazy persons are students. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: Students fall inside the hardworking group, which has no overlap with lazy persons.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red. Conclusions: I. Some roses are red. II. All red things are roses. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: The flowers that are red need not be roses.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Ravi is 7th from the left end and 12th from the right end in a row. How many persons are in the row?
questions.e: Total = position from left + position from right - 1 = 7 + 12 - 1 = 18.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a class of 40 students, Meena ranks 15th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?
questions.e: Rank from bottom = total - rank from top + 1 = 40 - 15 + 1 = 26th.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A is 5th from the left and B is 8th from the right. After they interchange positions, A becomes 12th from the left. How many persons are in the row?
questions.e: A's new left position (12) + B's right position (8) - 1 = 19.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a queue, Ramesh is 10th from the front and 20th from the back. How many people are in the queue?

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Sita is 3rd to the left of Gita, who is 8th from the right end in a row of 20 persons. What is Sita's position from the left end?
questions.e: Gita is 20 - 8 + 1 = 13th from the left, so Sita is 13 - 3 = 10th from the left.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: All phones are gadgets. Conclusion: Some gadgets are phones. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: If all phones are gadgets, then those phones are some of the gadgets.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: No honest person is corrupt. Conclusion: All corrupt persons are dishonest. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: The statement's contrapositive is that every corrupt person is not honest, i.e. dishonest.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: Some players are coaches. Conclusion: All coaches are players. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: 'Some' does not justify 'all'; the coaches who are not players break the conclusion.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: The best way to learn is to teach. Conclusion: Teaching improves one's own understanding. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: The conclusion is a direct restatement of the statement's claim.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: It is raining heavily. Conclusion: Everyone should carry an umbrella today. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: Heavy rain does not logically force everyone to carry an umbrella; it is advice, not a deduction.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Which diagram best represents the relationship between Dogs, Pets and Cats?
o: Two separate small circles (Dogs, Cats) inside a larger circle (Pets)
One circle inside another inside a third
questions.e: Some dogs and some cats are pets, but no dog is a cat; both groups sit inside the Pets circle.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Which diagram best represents the relationship between Fathers, Males and Doctors?
o: Fathers circle fully inside Males circle, overlapping Doctors circle
questions.e: All fathers are males, and some fathers and some males are doctors.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Which diagram best represents the relationship between India, Asia and Earth?
o: Three concentric circles: India inside Asia inside Earth
questions.e: India is a part of Asia, which is a part of the Earth - a clear subset chain.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A, B, C and D sit in a row facing north. C sits at the left end, A sits to the immediate left of B, and D sits to the immediate right of B. Who sits at the right end?
questions.e: The left-to-right order is C, A, B, D, so D is at the right end.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: P, Q, R and S sit in a row facing north. Q sits second from the left end and P sits second from the right end. R sits to the immediate right of Q. Who sits at the left end?
questions.e: The order is S, Q, R, P, so S is at the left end.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Five friends sit in a row facing north. Mohan sits in the middle. Ram sits to the immediate left of Mohan and Shyam to the immediate right of Mohan. Who sits second from the right end?
questions.e: The middle three are Ram, Mohan, Shyam; Shyam is second from the right end.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A, B, C and D sit in a circle facing the centre. A sits opposite B and C sits opposite D. If A is to the immediate left of C, who sits to the immediate right of C?
questions.e: With A opposite B and C opposite D, placing A to the left of C puts B to the right of C.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A 60-litre drum holds milk and water in the ratio 2:1. How many litres of water should be poured in so that the ratio becomes 5:4?
questions.e: Milk stays at 40 litres (60 × 2/3). For a 5:4 ratio with 40 litres of milk, water must be 40 × 4/5 = 32 litres; the drum already has 20, so 12 more litres are needed.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A grocer blends tea priced at Rs. 240 per kg with tea priced at Rs. 300 per kg to sell the blend at Rs. 270 per kg. In what ratio does he mix the two teas?
questions.e: By alligation, the cheaper tea's share : dearer tea's share = (300 − 270) : (270 − 240) = 30:30 = 1:1.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A tank holds 80 litres of pure milk. 16 litres are drawn off and replaced with water; then 16 litres of the resulting mixture are drawn off and replaced with water again. How much milk remains?
questions.e: After each replacement the milk left is multiplied by (1 − 16/80) = 0.8. After two rounds: 80 × 0.8² = 51.2 litres.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Two alloys contain copper and zinc in the ratios 2:3 and 4:1. In what ratio must they be melted together so that the new alloy has copper and zinc in the ratio 3:2?
questions.e: Copper fractions are 2/5, 4/5 and the target 3/5. By alligation: (4/5 − 3/5) : (3/5 − 2/5) = 1:1.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A milkman dilutes milk with water and sells the mixture at the cost price of pure milk, gaining 25% overall. What is the ratio of water to milk in the mixture?
questions.e: Selling at cost price, the gain comes entirely from the added water: gain% = (water/milk) × 100, so water:milk = 25:100 = 1:4.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Gold is 19 times as heavy as water and copper is 9 times as heavy as water. In what ratio should gold and copper be mixed to obtain an alloy 15 times as heavy as water?
questions.e: By alligation on relative density: gold's share : copper's share = (19 − 15) : (15 − 9) = 4:6 = 2:3.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A chemist mixes a 40% acid solution with a 70% acid solution. If she uses 30 litres of the 70% solution, how much of the 40% solution is needed to obtain a 52% solution?
questions.e: By alligation, 40%-solution : 70%-solution = (70 − 52) : (52 − 40) = 18:12 = 3:2. With 30 litres of the second, the first must be 30 × 3/2 = 45 litres.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A cask contains 50 litres of wine. 10 litres are drawn out and the cask is filled with water; the operation is repeated once more. How many litres of wine remain?
questions.e: Each operation leaves 4/5 of the wine: 50 × (4/5)² = 32 litres.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A 90 kg blend of sand and cement is in the ratio 4:5. How much cement must be added to change the ratio to 2:3?
questions.e: Sand is fixed at 90 × 4/9 = 40 kg. For 2:3, cement must be 40 × 3/2 = 60 kg; the blend has 50 kg, so 10 kg more are needed.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A merchant mixes rice costing Rs. 48 per kg with rice costing Rs. 60 per kg in the ratio 5:3 and sells the mixture at a 20% profit. What is the selling price per kg?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A dealer blends pulses costing Rs. 84 and Rs. 96 per kg. He sells the blend at Rs. 102.30 per kg, earning 10% profit. In what ratio did he mix the two pulses?
questions.e: Cost of the blend = 102.30/1.10 = Rs. 93 per kg. By alligation, cheaper : dearer = (96 − 93) : (93 − 84) = 3:9 = 1:3.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A vessel holds milk and water in the ratio 5:3. When 16 litres of the mixture are removed and replaced with 16 litres of water, the ratio becomes 1:1. What was the original quantity?
questions.e: Let the total be x litres. Milk removed = 16 × 5/8 = 10 L, water removed = 6 L. Then 5x/8 − 10 = 3x/8 − 6 + 16, giving 2x/8 = 20, so x = 80 litres.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A shopkeeper has 100 kg of sugar, part sold at 10% profit and the rest at 20% profit, with an overall gain of 14%. How much did he sell at 10% profit?
questions.e: By alligation, the 10%-lot : 20%-lot = (20 − 14) : (14 − 10) = 6:4 = 3:2. So 100 × 3/5 = 60 kg was sold at 10% profit.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A 100-litre cask contains spirit and water in the ratio 7:3. How much spirit must be added to make the ratio 4:1?
questions.e: Water is fixed at 30 litres. For a 4:1 ratio, spirit must be 30 × 4 = 120 litres; the cask has 70, so 50 litres are added.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Three jars hold milk and water in the ratios 2:3, 3:2 and 5:1. Equal quantities from the three jars are mixed. What fraction of the final mixture is milk?
questions.e: Milk fractions are 2/5, 3/5 and 5/6. Their mean is (2/5 + 3/5 + 5/6)/3 = (11/6)/3 = 11/18.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If 35% of a number is 140, what is 65% of the same number?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: After taking the principal square roots, determine √3.24 + √0.81 − √1.21.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Evaluate (1.2)² − (0.8)².

questions.subject: Quant
questions.e: Division and multiplication first: 9 × 3 = 27 and 6 ÷ 2 = 3. Then 27 − 15 + 3 = 15.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Calculate the sum of three-fifths of 245 and two-sevenths of 336.
questions.e: 3/5 of 245 = 147 and 2/7 of 336 = 96. Their sum is 243.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Use the identity for a perfect square to compute 999 × 999 + 2 × 999 + 1.
questions.e: This is (999 + 1)² by the identity a² + 2a + 1 = (a + 1)², giving 1000² = 1,000,000.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The sum of ∛1331 and ∛3375 equals:

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is √(5² + 12² + 2 × 5 × 12) equal to?
questions.e: The radicand is (5 + 12)² = 17² by the identity a² + b² + 2ab, so the square root is 17.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Using the sum-of-cubes identity, determine (0.75³ + 0.25³) ÷ (0.75² − 0.75 × 0.25 + 0.25²).
questions.e: Using (a³ + b³) = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²), the division collapses to a + b = 0.75 + 0.25 = 1.00.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above cost price but allows a 15% discount. What is his profit percentage?
questions.e: Take cost as 100: marked price 140, selling price 140 × 0.85 = 119, a gain of 19%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What single discount is equivalent to two successive discounts of 20% and 25%?
questions.e: Successive discounts multiply: 0.80 × 0.75 = 0.60, so the customer pays 60%, an effective discount of 40%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: An article marked at Rs. 2,500 is sold after successive discounts of 12% and 8%. What is the selling price?
questions.e: 2500 × 0.88 = 2200 after the first discount; 2200 × 0.92 = 2024 after the second.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: An article costs Rs. 1,200 and is marked 25% above cost. If it is sold at a 10% discount, what is the profit percentage?
questions.e: Marked price = 1500, selling price = 1500 × 0.90 = 1350, profit = 150 on 1200 = 12.5%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Which offer is better for the buyer: a single 30% discount or two successive discounts of 15% each?
questions.e: Two successive 15% discounts leave 0.85 × 0.85 = 0.7225 of the price, i.e. only 27.75% off — less than a flat 30% discount.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: After a 20% discount, a shirt sells for Rs. 640. What was its marked price?
questions.e: Marked price × 0.80 = 640, so marked price = 640 ÷ 0.80 = Rs. 800.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is the single equivalent of three successive discounts of 10%, 20% and 30%?
questions.e: 0.90 × 0.80 × 0.70 = 0.504 remains, so the effective discount is 1 − 0.504 = 49.6%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A dealer gives a 5% cash discount and still earns 14% profit on an article costing Rs. 800. What is its marked price?
questions.e: Selling price = 800 × 1.14 = 912. Marked price × 0.95 = 912 gives marked price = 912 ÷ 0.95 = Rs. 960.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If 2x + 3y = 12 and x − y = 1, what is the value of x?
questions.e: From x − y = 1, x = y + 1. Substituting: 2(y + 1) + 3y = 12 gives 5y = 10, so y = 2 and x = 3.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If a + b = 9 and ab = 20, what is the value of a² + b²?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If x − y = 5 and xy = 36, what is the value of x² + y²?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If p + q + r = 0, what does p³ + q³ + r³ equal?
questions.e: The identity p³ + q³ + r³ − 3pqr = (p + q + r)(...) gives p³ + q³ + r³ = 3pqr when the sum is zero.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If 2x + 3y = 17 and 3x + 2y = 18, what is x + y?
questions.e: Adding the two equations gives 5x + 5y = 35, so x + y = 7.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is the value of [(a − b)³ + (b − c)³ + (c − a)³] ÷ [(a − b)(b − c)(c − a)]?
questions.e: Since (a−b) + (b−c) + (c−a) = 0, the numerator equals 3(a−b)(b−c)(c−a), and the division gives 3.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If x² + 1/x² = 27 and x > 1/x, what is the positive value of x − 1/x?
questions.e: (x − 1/x)² = x² + 1/x² − 2 = 25, and with x > 1/x the value is the positive root 5.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If a:b = 3:4 and b:c = 8:9, what is a:c?
questions.e: Make b common: a:b = 6:8 and b:c = 8:9, so a:b:c = 6:8:9 and a:c = 6:9 = 2:3.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is an acute angle, what is tan θ?
questions.e: cos θ = 4/5 from the 3-4-5 triangle, so tan θ = sin θ/cos θ = 3/4.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is the value of sin²30° + cos²30° + tan²45°?
questions.e: sin²30° + cos²30° = 1 by the Pythagorean identity, and tan 45° = 1, so the total is 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If tan A = 1 and A is acute, what is the measure of angle A?
questions.e: tan 45° = 1, and for acute angles the tangent is one-to-one, so A = 45°.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Evaluate: sin 60° · cos 30° + cos 60° · sin 30°.
questions.e: This is sin(60° + 30°) = sin 90° = 1 by the angle-addition formula.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If sec θ − tan θ = 1/3, what is sec θ + tan θ?
questions.e: Since (sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, the required value is 1 ÷ (1/3) = 3.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Simplify: (1 − sin²θ)(1 + tan²θ).
questions.e: 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ and 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; their product is cos²θ · sec²θ = 1.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If cosec θ = 13/5 and θ is acute, what is cot θ?
questions.e: From the 5-12-13 triangle, sin θ = 5/13 gives cos θ = 12/13, so cot θ = 12/5.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If θ = 30°, what is the value of 2sin²θ + 3cos²θ?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A factory's output (in thousand units) was: 2022 – 45, 2023 – 54, 2024 – 63, 2025 – 72. What was the percentage increase in output from 2022 to 2025?
questions.e: Increase = 72 − 45 = 27 on a base of 45, giving 27/45 × 100 = 60%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Wheat production (lakh tonnes) in 2024 and 2025 was: State P – 40 and 52; State Q – 60 and 72; State R – 50 and 60. Which state recorded the highest percentage increase in 2025?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A pie chart of monthly expenses shows: Food 108°, Rent 90°, Transport 54°, Others 108°. What percentage of income is spent on transport?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A shop's daily customers were: Mon 120, Tue 150, Wed 90, Thu 180, Fri 160. On how many days did the customer count exceed the five-day average?
questions.e: Total = 700, average = 140; Tue (150), Thu (180) and Fri (160) exceed it — 3 days.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A student's marks (each paper out of 100) are: English 72, Maths 85, Science 68, Hindi 75. What is her overall percentage?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A town's population (in thousands) was: 2020 – 240, 2021 – 264, 2022 – 297. In which interval was the absolute increase the greatest?
questions.e: 2020–21: +24 thousand; 2021–22: +33 thousand — the later interval is greater.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A batter's first five innings scores are 45, 0, 78, 32 and 55. After the sixth innings his average becomes 42. What did he score in the sixth innings?
questions.e: First five total 210; six innings at average 42 need 252, so the sixth innings = 252 − 210 = 42.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A survey of 200 families recorded vehicles owned: 0 vehicles – 30 families, 1 – 90, 2 – 60, 3 or more – 20. What is the median number of vehicles per family?
questions.e: Cumulative counts reach 30, then 120; the 100th and 101st families both fall in the '1 vehicle' group, so the median is 1.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A country's exports (Rs. crore) were 150 in 2021 and 180 in 2022; imports were 120 and 160. How did the trade surplus change from 2021 to 2022?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A company has 1,500 employees: 40% in Production, 25% in Sales, 20% in R&D and the rest in Admin. How many employees are in Admin?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Monthly rainfall (mm) was: June 120, July 180, August 150, September 90. What fraction of the four-month total fell in July?
questions.e: Total = 540 mm; July's 180 mm is 180/540 = 1/3 of the total.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: School A: 120 of 150 students passed; School B: 200 of 250 passed. What is the combined pass percentage of the two schools?
questions.e: Passed = 320 out of 400 students = 320/400 × 100 = 80%.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, forming an interior angle of 65°. What is the measure of its corresponding angle?
questions.e: Corresponding angles formed by a transversal on parallel lines are equal, so the corresponding angle is also 65°.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: In triangle ABC, AB = AC and angle A = 40°. What is angle B?
questions.e: AB = AC makes it isosceles with ∠B = ∠C; (180 − 40)/2 = 70°.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A circle has radius 7 cm. What is its area? (Take π = 22/7)

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The diagonal of a square measures 10√2 cm. What is the side of the square?
questions.e: Diagonal = side × √2, so side = 10√2/√2 = 10 cm.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A right-angled triangle has legs of 9 cm and 12 cm. What is its hypotenuse?

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a class of 60 students, 35 like cricket, 28 like football and 10 like both games. How many students like neither game?
questions.e: Students liking at least one game = 35 + 28 − 10 = 53. Those liking neither = 60 − 53 = 7.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a class of 100 students, 50 like Maths, 45 like Science and 40 like English; 18 like Maths and Science, 14 like Science and English, 12 like Maths and English, and 6 like all three. How many students like none of the three subjects?
questions.e: By inclusion–exclusion, at least one = 50 + 45 + 40 − 18 − 14 − 12 + 6 = 97. None = 100 − 97 = 3.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A survey of 200 people found 120 like tea, 90 like coffee and 50 like both. How many like exactly one of the two?
questions.e: Only tea = 120 − 50 = 70; only coffee = 90 − 50 = 40. Exactly one = 70 + 40 = 110.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a group of 50 people, 32 like tea and 28 like coffee. What is the smallest possible number of people who like both?
questions.e: The overlap is smallest when the two groups are spread out as much as possible: 32 + 28 − 50 = 10.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a colony, 60% of residents own a car, 50% own a two-wheeler and 25% own both. What percentage owns exactly one type of vehicle?
questions.e: Only car = 60 − 25 = 35%; only two-wheeler = 50 − 25 = 25%. Exactly one = 35 + 25 = 60%.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: A survey of 100 people reports that 70 like tea, 65 like coffee, 50 like both and 20 like neither. What follows from these figures?
o: Everyone likes at least one drink
questions.e: At least one drink = 70 + 65 − 50 = 85; adding the 20 who like neither gives 105, which exceeds the 100 people surveyed — impossible.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a factory, 40% of workers use bus A, 35% use bus B and 15% use both buses. What percentage uses neither bus?
questions.e: At least one bus = 40 + 35 − 15 = 60%. Neither = 100 − 60 = 40%.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a group of 72 people, those who like tea only, coffee only and both are in the ratio 3:2:1, and 12 people like neither drink. How many people like both drinks?
questions.e: Let the parts be 3x, 2x and x: 3x + 2x + x + 12 = 72 gives x = 10, so both = 10.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In an election survey of 200 voters, 130 support candidate X, 110 support candidate Y and 40 support neither. How many support both?

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Of 120 students, 70 study Hindi, 60 study English and 50 study Sanskrit; 30 study Hindi and English, 25 study English and Sanskrit, 20 study Hindi and Sanskrit, and 10 study all three. How many study exactly one language?
questions.e: Only Hindi = 70 − 30 − 20 + 10 = 30; only English = 60 − 30 − 25 + 10 = 15; only Sanskrit = 50 − 25 − 20 + 10 = 15. Exactly one = 30 + 15 + 15 = 60.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a colony of 72 families, 45 like reading, 38 like gardening and 12 like neither hobby. How many families like exactly one hobby?

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a company, 75% of the 200 employees own a smartphone; of the remaining employees, half own a basic mobile phone. How many employees own no phone at all?
questions.e: No smartphone = 25% of 200 = 50 employees; half of these (25) own a basic phone, leaving 50 − 25 = 25 with no phone.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Ten people sit in two parallel rows facing each other. P, Q, R, S and T sit in Row 1, while A, B, C, D and E sit in Row 2; each person faces exactly one person in the other row (position 1 faces position 1, and so on, numbering 1 to 5 from the left). P sits at the left end of Row 1 and faces A. Q sits at the right end of Row 1 and faces C. S sits next to P. R sits between S and Q. T sits between R and Q. D sits next to C. Who faces D?
questions.e: Row 1 from the left: P (1, left end), S (2, next to P), R (3, between S and Q), T (4, between R and Q), Q (5, right end). C faces Q, so C is Row 2 position 5; D sits next to C at position 4, facing Row 1's position 4 — T.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Five children A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north. C sits in the middle. A sits second to the left of C. B sits immediately to the right of A. D sits at an end. Who sits immediately to the left of D?
questions.e: Positions left to right: A(1), B(2), C(3), E(4), D(5) — D must take the free end at position 5, leaving E at 4. D faces north, so his own left is the lower-numbered side: the person immediately to D's left is E at position 4.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Eight colleagues P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W sit around a circular table facing the centre. P sits opposite T. Q sits second to the left of P. R sits immediately to the right of Q. S sits opposite R. V sits between T and Q. W sits immediately to the right of P. Who sits second to the right of V?
questions.e: With P as reference: T opposite P; Q two places anti-clockwise from P; R one place clockwise from Q; S opposite R; V the single seat between T and Q; W one place clockwise from P; U fills the last seat. V's seat has R two places clockwise from it.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Six people M, N, O, P, Q and R sit in a row facing north. M sits third from the left end. N sits immediately to the right of M. O sits at the right end. P sits between N and O. Q sits immediately to the left of M. Who sits at the left end?
questions.e: M = 3, N = 4, O = 6, P = 5 (between N and O), Q = 2 (left of M). The only seat left, position 1, goes to R.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Six people A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table. A, C and E face the centre, while B, D and F face outward. B sits second to the left of A. D sits immediately to the right of B. F sits opposite D. C sits immediately to the right of A. Who sits immediately to the right of C?
questions.e: Number seats 0–5 clockwise with A at 0, facing the centre. A centre-facing person's left is clockwise, so B is at 2. B faces outward; an outward-facing person's right is counter-clockwise, so D is at 1. F sits opposite D at 4 (and indeed faces outward). C sits immediately right of A — a centre-facing person's right is counter-clockwise — at 5, leaving E at 3. Immediately right of C (counter-clockwise from 5) is seat 4 — F.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row facing north. D sits fourth from the left. A sits second to the right of D. G sits at the left end. E sits immediately to the right of G. B sits between E and D. C sits immediately to the left of A. Who sits third from the right end?
questions.e: Left to right: G(1), E(2), B(3), D(4), C(5), A(6), F(7). Counting from the right end, the third seat is C.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Six people P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a row facing north. Each likes a different fruit: apple, banana, mango, orange, pear or grape. P sits second from the left end and likes mango. Q sits at the right end. The person who likes apple sits immediately to the left of Q. R sits between P and the person who likes apple. S likes banana and sits immediately to the right of R. T likes grape and sits at the left end. The person who likes pear sits immediately to the right of P. Who likes orange?
questions.e: Positions 1–6: T at 1 (grape); P at 2 (mango); the pear-lover at 3 (immediately right of P); the apple-lover at 5 (immediately left of Q at 6); R sits strictly between P (2) and the apple-lover (5) — R cannot be at 4, because then S (immediately right of R, banana) would clash with the apple-lover at 5 — so R is at 3 (pear) and S at 4 (banana); U is the apple-lover at 5. The only unassigned fruit, orange, goes to Q.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Five people P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. Q sits in the middle. P sits second to the left of Q. R sits immediately to the right of P. S sits at an end. Who sits between Q and S?
questions.e: Positions: P(1), R(2), Q(3), T(4), S(5) — S takes the free end at 5, leaving T at 4. Between Q(3) and S(5) sits T.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Five friends Aman, Bina, Chetan, Deepak and Esha live on five floors of a building (1 = ground floor, 5 = top). Aman lives on the top floor. Bina lives immediately below Aman. Chetan lives two floors below Bina. Deepak lives above Esha. Who lives on the ground floor?
questions.e: Aman = 5, Bina = 4, Chetan = 2. Of the remaining floors 1 and 3, Deepak must be above Esha, so Deepak = 3 and Esha = 1 (ground floor).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Four colleagues P, Q, R and S live on floors 1 to 4 of a hostel. P lives on an even-numbered floor. Q lives immediately above P. R lives below S. Who lives on floor 4?
questions.e: P must be on floor 2 (floor 4 would push Q to a non-existent floor 5), so Q = 3. R below S on floors 1 and 4 gives R = 1, S = 4.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Eight people A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H sit around a square table facing the centre, two on each side. A sits at a corner. B sits immediately to the right of A. C sits opposite B. D sits at a corner immediately to the left of C. E sits between A and G. Who sits immediately to the left of G?
questions.e: Number the seats 0–7 clockwise; even seats are corners. A is at corner 0; for a centre-facing person right is counter-clockwise, so B is at 7; C sits opposite B at 3; left of a centre-facing person is clockwise, so D (a corner) is at 4; E sits between A (0) and G — the only free seat adjacent to A is 1 (7 is taken), so E is at 1 and G at 2. Immediately left of G (clockwise from 2) is seat 3 — C.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Six people U, V, W, X, Y and Z sit in a row facing north. X sits at the left end. Y sits third from the right end. W sits immediately to the left of Y. V sits at the right end. Who sits immediately to the right of W?
questions.e: X = 1, Y = 4 (third from the right in six seats), W = 3, V = 6, leaving Z = 2 and U = 5. The seat right of W(3) is Y(4).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Six friends P, Q, R, S, T and U sit around a circular table facing the centre. P sits second to the left of Q. R sits opposite P. S sits immediately to the right of R. U sits immediately to the left of Q. Who sits opposite T?
questions.e: With Q as reference: P two places anti-clockwise; R opposite P; S one place clockwise from R; U one place anti-clockwise from Q; T fills the last seat, which is opposite Q.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Five people P, Q, R, S and T sit in a row facing north. Each has a different occupation: doctor, engineer, teacher, lawyer and artist. R is the engineer and sits in the middle. The doctor sits second to the left of the engineer. P is the lawyer and sits at the right end. The teacher sits immediately to the left of P. Q sits next to the doctor. Who is the artist?
questions.e: R (engineer) in the middle is position 3; the doctor is two places left at position 1; P (lawyer) at the right end is position 5; the teacher immediately left of P is position 4; Q sits next to the doctor (position 1), so Q is at position 2. The only occupation left for position 2 is artist — Q.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a line of people, Arjun is 12th from the left and 29th from the right. How many people are in the line?
questions.e: Total = position from left + position from right − 1 = 12 + 29 − 1 = 40.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a queue of 50 people, Meera is 18th from the front. What is her position from the back?
questions.e: Position from the back = total − position from front + 1 = 50 − 18 + 1 = 33rd.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Five books are stacked one above the other. The Hindi book is above the English book; the Maths book is below the English book but above the Science book; the History book is at the bottom. Which book is on the top?
questions.e: The chain Hindi > English > Maths > Science with History at the bottom gives top-to-bottom order Hindi, English, Maths, Science, History.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a class, Rohan ranks 7th from the top and 24th from the bottom. What is the strength of the class?
questions.e: Strength = 7 + 24 − 1 = 30.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: P is heavier than Q, R is heavier than P, S is lighter than Q, and T is heavier than R. Who is the heaviest?
questions.e: The chain is S < Q < P < R < T, so T is the heaviest.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Amit is 15th from the left end and 20th from the right end of a row. If 5 people join at the right end, what becomes Amit's position from the right?
questions.e: Adding 5 people at the right end pushes every right-end count up by 5: 20 + 5 = 25th.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Kiran is 8th from the left and 11th from the right in a row. How many people stand between Kiran and the person who is 5th from the right?
questions.e: Total = 8 + 11 − 1 = 18. The 5th from the right is 14th from the left. Between positions 8 and 14 lie 5 people.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Five runners P, Q, R, S and T finish a race. P finishes ahead of Q. R finishes ahead of P. S finishes immediately after R. T finishes last. Who finishes third?
questions.e: R ahead of P with S immediately after R fixes the order R, S, P; Q follows P and T is last: R, S, P, Q, T. Third is P.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Some children stand in a row. Rahul is 14th from the left end and 9th from the right end. How many children are in the row?

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Among five friends, Divya is taller than Esha, Esha is taller than Farah, Gita is taller than Divya, and Hina is the shortest. Who is the tallest?
questions.e: The chain is Hina < Farah < Esha < Divya < Gita, so Gita is the tallest.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: All sparrows are birds. Conclusion: Some birds are sparrows. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: If every sparrow is a bird, then the set of birds certainly contains sparrows, so some birds are sparrows.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: No fish lives on land. Conclusion: All land animals are not fish. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: Since no fish lives on land, anything living on land cannot be a fish — the conclusion is the contrapositive of the statement.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: Some engineers are designers. Conclusion: All designers are engineers. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: 'Some' works in only one direction: the statement says nothing about designers who are not engineers.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: Reading daily improves vocabulary. Conclusion: Everyone who reads daily has an excellent vocabulary. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: Improvement is a tendency, not a guarantee of excellence for every individual — the conclusion overstates the statement.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: All squares are rectangles. Conclusion: Some rectangles are squares. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: Every square being a rectangle means the rectangle family includes squares, so some rectangles are squares.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: No cricketer is a footballer. Conclusion: Some footballers are cricketers. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: The conclusion directly contradicts the statement, which excludes all overlap between the two groups.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: Honesty is the best policy. Conclusion: Dishonest people never succeed in life. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: Praising honesty says nothing about whether dishonest people can succeed — the conclusion adds an unsupported absolute.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statement: All roses are flowers. Conclusion: No rose is a flower. Does the conclusion follow?
questions.e: The conclusion is the exact negation of the statement, so it cannot follow from it.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All tables are furniture. All furniture is wood. Conclusions: I. All tables are wood. II. Some wood is furniture. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: Tables sit inside furniture, which sits inside wood, so all tables are wood. Reversing the second statement, some wood (the furniture part) is furniture.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: Some novels are classics. All classics are literature. Conclusions: I. Some novels are literature. II. All literature is classics. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: The novels that are classics lie inside literature, so the first conclusion holds; but literature extends beyond classics, so the second does not.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: No desert is fertile. All fertile lands are farmed. Conclusions: I. No desert is farmed. II. Some farmed lands are fertile. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: A desert could still be farmed without being fertile, so the first conclusion overreaches; the second is just the reverse of the second statement and is valid.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All athletes are fit. No fit person is inactive. Conclusions: I. No athlete is inactive. II. Some inactive persons are athletes. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: Athletes are inside the fit group, which has no overlap with the inactive group, so no athlete is inactive; the second conclusion contradicts this.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All rivers are water. Some water is salty. No salty thing is drinkable. Conclusions: I. Some rivers are drinkable. II. No water is drinkable. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: Nothing links rivers to the salty part of water, so the first conclusion is unsupported; only salty water is undrinkable, so the second overgeneralises.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All computers are machines. Some machines are expensive. Conclusions: I. Some computers are expensive. II. All expensive things are machines. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: The expensive machines may lie entirely outside the computer part, and expensive things in general need not be machines at all.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: Some teachers are mentors. All mentors are guides. Conclusions: I. Some teachers are guides. II. Some guides are teachers. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: The teachers who are mentors sit inside the guide group, giving the first conclusion; reversing it, some guides (those mentors) are teachers.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: No square is a circle. Some circles are shapes. Conclusions: I. Some shapes are not squares. II. No shape is a square. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: The shapes that are circles cannot be squares, so the first conclusion holds; but other shapes might still be squares, so the second overreaches.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Statements: All keys are locks. Some locks are doors. Conclusions: I. Some keys are doors. II. No key is a door. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.e: No definite link between keys and doors can be drawn, but the two conclusions are exact contradictories, so one of them must be true.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Four spellings of one word are given. Select the correct spelling: 'discipline'.
questions.e: The correct spelling is d-i-s-c-i-p-l-i-n-e: 'discipline'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In the sentence 'The ___ of the new bridge took nearly two years', which spelling of the noun is correct?
questions.e: The correct spelling is 'construction'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Identify the misspelt word among the options: 'perseverance'.
questions.e: The correct spelling is 'perseverance' (per-se-ver-ance).

questions.subject: English
questions.q: From the options below, pick the word with no spelling error:
questions.e: The correct spelling is 'recognition'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Spot the correctly spelt word:
questions.e: The correct spelling is 'consensus'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The sentence with the blank — "The patient was waiting for the doctor's ___" — needs the correct noun form. Choose it.
questions.e: The noun form is 'diagnosis'; 'diagnoses' is the verb/plural form and does not fit the singular blank.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the word with the correct spelling:
questions.e: The correct spelling is 'exhibition'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Only one option below is spelt correctly. Pick it out.
questions.e: The correct spelling is 'evidence'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word for the blank: 'The committee submitted its ___ to the chairman.'
questions.e: The correct spelling is 'recommendation' (double m, single c).

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct indirect-speech form of: She said, "I have finished my homework."
o: She said that she had finished her homework.
She said that she finished her homework yesterday.
She says that she had finished her homework.
She said that she has finished her homework.
questions.e: Present perfect in reported speech shifts to past perfect, and 'my' becomes 'her': she had finished her homework.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which sentence correctly reports this universal truth? The teacher said, "The sun rises in the east."
o: The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.
The teacher says that the sun rises in the east.
The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.
The teacher said that the sun had risen in the east.
questions.e: Universal truths keep the present tense in indirect speech; only the quotation marks and 'that' change.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Spot the error-free reported version of: He said to her, "Will you help me?"
o: He said to her that she would help me.
He asked her if she will help me.
He asked her whether she would help him.
He told her that will she help him.
questions.e: Yes/no questions become 'asked ... if/whether' clauses; 'will' shifts to 'would', 'you' to 'she', 'me' to 'him'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Apply the reported-speech rule to the imperative: "Don't touch the exhibits," the guard said.
o: The guard says not to touch the exhibits.
The guard forbade them to touch the exhibits.
The guard said to not touch the exhibits.
The guard told them not to touch the exhibits.
questions.e: Imperatives in the negative become 'told/ordered ... not to' + base verb.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Select the correct conversion into indirect speech: She said, "I was watching a movie last night."
o: She said that she has been watching a movie the previous night.
She said that she had been watching a movie the previous night.
She said that she watched a movie last night.
She said that she was watching a movie last night.
questions.e: Past continuous shifts to past perfect continuous, and 'last night' becomes 'the previous night'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Identify the correctly reported sentence for: He said, "I shall meet you tomorrow."
o: He said that he would meet me the next day.
He said that he will meet you the next day.
He said that he shall meet me tomorrow.
He says that he would meet me tomorrow.
questions.e: 'Shall' becomes 'would' in reported speech, 'you' becomes 'me', and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Improve the sentence: She is senior than me in service.
o: She is senior to me in service.
She is senior than me in service.
She is senior from me in service.
She is more senior than me in service.
questions.e: The adjectives senior, junior, superior and inferior take the preposition 'to', not 'than'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Improve the sentence: The news are not good today.
o: The news are not good today.
The news is not good today.
The news have not been good today.
The news were not good today.
questions.e: 'News' is a singular noun despite its -s ending, so it takes a singular verb.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Improve the sentence: He ordered for two cups of tea.
o: He ordered for two cups of tea.
He ordered two cups of tea.
He had ordered for two cups of tea.
He ordered to two cups of tea.
questions.e: The verb 'order' does not take 'for' before its object in this construction.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Improve the sentence: One must do his duty sincerely.
o: One must do his duty sincerely.
One must do their duty sincerely.
One must do its duty sincerely.
One must do one's duty sincerely.
questions.e: The indefinite pronoun 'one' is followed by 'one's', not 'his' or 'their'.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The Durand Cup, Asia's oldest football tournament, was first held in:
questions.e: The Durand Cup began in 1888 and is Asia's oldest football tournament.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: Who was the first Indian to win an individual Olympic medal?
questions.e: Khashaba Jadhav won a wrestling bronze at Helsinki 1952, India's first individual Olympic medal.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: Neeraj Chopra won India's first Olympic gold medal in athletics at:
questions.e: Neeraj Chopra's javelin gold at Tokyo 2020 was India's first Olympic gold in athletics.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The Wimbledon tennis championship is played on which surface?
questions.e: Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam still played on grass courts.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The Subroto Cup is associated with which sport?
questions.e: The Subroto Cup is an inter-school football tournament of India.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: Which country won the ICC Cricket World Cup 2023?
questions.e: Australia defeated India in the final at Ahmedabad to win the 2023 ODI World Cup.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The 2022 Asian Games were hosted by which city?
questions.e: The 2022 Asian Games, held in 2023, were hosted by Hangzhou, China.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The novel 'Godan' was written by:
questions.e: 'Godan' (1936) is the most celebrated novel of Munshi Premchand.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The novel 'The Guide' was written by:
questions.e: 'The Guide' (1958) is a classic by R. K. Narayan.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: 'Train to Pakistan' is a novel by:
questions.e: 'Train to Pakistan' (1956) on the Partition was written by Khushwant Singh.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: 'The White Tiger', which won the Man Booker Prize in 2008, was written by:
questions.e: Aravind Adiga's debut novel 'The White Tiger' won the 2008 Man Booker Prize.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier-I examination is scheduled to be held during which period?
questions.e: As announced by the Staff Selection Commission in September 2026, the CGL 2026 Tier-I computer-based exam runs from 30 September to 30 October 2026 for 12,256 Group B & C posts.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: Who won India's first shooting gold at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games?
o: Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar & Sift Kaur
questions.e: On 25 September 2026, Suruchi Inder Singh and Kamaljeet won gold in the 10m air pistol mixed team event, setting an Asian record — India's first shooting gold of the Games.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: Under Tamil Nadu's 'Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam', launched on 28 September 2026, each eligible newborn receives:
questions.e: The scheme gifts a one-gram, 22-carat gold ring with a unique serial number to every newborn delivered in a Tamil Nadu government hospital; the first phase covers 1.28 lakh rings.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: In which event did Gulveer Singh win a silver medal at the 2026 Asian Games on 25 September 2026?
questions.e: Gulveer Singh won silver in the men's 10,000m, becoming the first Indian to win multiple 10,000m medals in Asian Games history.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A man's salary increases from ₹40,000 to ₹48,000. What is the percentage increase?

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the next term in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.e: The differences increase by 2 each time (4, 6, 8, 10, 12); so the next term is 30 + 12 = 42. Equivalently n(n+1): 1×2, 2×3, … 6×7 = 42.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom 'at the eleventh hour':
questions.e: 'At the eleventh hour' means at the latest possible moment before it is too late.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: The average of five numbers is 27. If one number is excluded, the average of the remaining four becomes 25. What is the excluded number?
questions.e: Total of the five = 5 × 27 = 135; total of the four = 4 × 25 = 100; excluded = 135 − 100 = 35.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-I admit cards are being released:
o: In phases, about 2-3 days before each candidate’s exam date
Only after Tier-I results are declared
Through post offices by speed post
questions.e: SSC releases admission certificates in phases; each candidate’s admit card goes live roughly 2-3 days before their CBT date (30 Sep–30 Oct 2026).

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: Who was appointed Chairperson of the CBSE in September 2026?
questions.e: The ACC approved Mandeep K. Bhandari (2001-batch AGMUT IAS) as CBSE Chairperson; he replaces Lokhande Prashant Sitaram, who held additional charge.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: In its September 2026 Interim Economic Outlook, the OECD raised India’s FY27 GDP growth forecast to:
questions.e: OECD’s ‘Weathering Successive Shocks’ (Sep 2026) raised FY27 growth by 80 bps to 7.1% from 6.3% projected in June.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: At the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026, Esha Singh won the silver medal in:
questions.e: Esha Singh finished second in the women’s 25m pistol final on 28 September 2026, losing a shoot-off to China’s Xiao Jiaruixian.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: India’s best-ever finish at the WorldSkills competition came at Shanghai 2026, where India placed:
questions.e: India placed 10th at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 with six silvers and 20 Medals for Excellence — its best show ever, up from 13th at Lyon 2024.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to: Resilient
questions.e: Resilient means able to recover quickly from difficulties; tough and flexible.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: If 28,52,665 candidates appear for an exam and 12,256 posts are filled, the selection ratio is closest to:
questions.e: 28,52,665 ÷ 12,256 ≈ 233, so roughly one post for every 233 candidates.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: In a certain code language, EXAM is written as FYBN. How will TEST be written?
questions.e: Each letter shifts +1: E→F, X→Y, A→B, M→N. So T→U, E→F, S→T, T→U = UFTU.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: SSC released the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 admit cards in phases beginning on which date, ahead of the exam starting 30 September 2026?
questions.e: Admit cards were issued in phases from 27 September 2026 (for the 30 September shift first); the Tier 1 CBE runs 30 September to 30 October 2026.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: As per the SSC 2026-27 calendar, the Constable (GD) 2027 computer-based exam is scheduled in:
questions.e: The calendar places the GD Constable 2027 CBE in January-March 2027, with the notification expected in September 2026 and applications open into October.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The SSC CHSL 2026 application window (opened 7 September 2026) closes on:
questions.e: CHSL 2026 applications close on 7 October 2026 at 11 pm; fee payment till 8 October and the correction window on 14-16 October. The notice covers about 2,536 LDC/JSA and DEO posts.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 comprises how many questions and marks?
questions.e: Tier 1 has 100 MCQs - 25 each from General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Awareness, Quantitative Aptitude and English Comprehension - of 2 marks each (200 marks), in 60 minutes.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: Under the sliding mechanism used in SSC results (e.g. Stenographer Grade C and D 2026), a FLOAT option means the candidate:
o: may be considered for a better preference if vacancies arise
is moved to the next exam cycle
questions.e: FLOAT lets a candidate be considered for a higher-preference post if vacancies arise from non-joining; FIX accepts the current allocation.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: In SSC CGL 2026, the new Tier 2 Paper-III is meant for candidates applying to:
questions.e: The CGL 2026 pattern added Paper-III in Tier 2 only for Junior Statistical Officer (JSO) posts in the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The Staff Selection Commission was established in which year?
questions.e: The Staff Selection Commission was set up in 1975 (originally as the Subordinate Services Commission) and is headquartered in New Delhi.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The official website for SSC registrations, applications, admit cards and results is:
questions.e: All new registrations, applications, admit cards and results are handled at ssc.gov.in; the old ssc.nic.in portal no longer supports One-Time Registration.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-1 prescribes negative marking of:
questions.e: Tier-1 has 100 questions for 200 marks, a 60-minute duration and 0.50 negative marking per wrong answer.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: How many vacancies were tentatively notified for SSC CGL 2026?
questions.e: SSC CGL 2026 notified about 12,256 vacancies; Tier-1 runs 30 September–30 October 2026.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The last date to apply online for SSC CHSL 2026 is:
questions.e: CHSL 2026 (2,536 posts) applications close 7 October 2026; corrections are allowed 14–16 October 2026.

questions.subject: GA
questions.q: The India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement comes into force on:
questions.e: Announced as a landmark pact signed in May 2026, the India–NZ FTA takes effect from 20 October 2026.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to ADAMANT:
questions.e: Adamant means refusing to be persuaded — 'stubborn' is the closest synonym.

questions.subject: Quant
questions.q: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.e: SI for doubling = P; R = (100 × P)/(P × 8) = 12.5% per annum.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 3, 9, 27, 81, ?
questions.e: Each term is multiplied by 3: 81 × 3 = 243.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: SSC CHSL (10+2) 2026 notifies how many tentative vacancies?
questions.e: 2,536 tentative posts; applications 7 September-7 October 2026 on ssc.gov.in.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Neeru Dhanda won gold in the women's individual trap at the 2026 Asian Games, becoming:
o: The first Indian woman to win individual Asian Games gold in trap
questions.e: Her trap gold was the first individual Asian Games gold for an Indian woman in the event.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: India's Index of Industrial Production grew ___ year-on-year in August 2026.
questions.e: IIP grew 8.0% YoY in August 2026, with manufacturing up 9.0%.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The World Heart Day 2026 campaign theme was:
questions.e: World Heart Day was observed on 29 September 2026 with the theme 'Don't Miss a Beat'.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 'three mutuals' guiding India-China ties are:
o: Mutual respect, mutual interest, mutual sensitivity
Mutual trade, mutual defence, mutual aid
Mutual trust, mutual benefit, mutual security
Mutual dialogue, mutual visits, mutual treaties
questions.e: The MEA said ties are taken forward under mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: EOS-05 is reported as India's first imaging satellite designed for:
questions.e: EOS-05 (launched 4 Sep 2026 on GSLV-F17 into Sub-GTO) is India's first imaging satellite designed for geosynchronous orbit.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Vithya Ramraj's 54.75s 400m hurdles bronze broke a national record (55.42s, 1984) held by:
questions.e: Vithya Ramraj broke P.T. Usha's 55.42-second national record from 1984.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine advanced the field of:
questions.e: Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel — light-gated ion channels; announced 5 Oct 2026.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: The IceCube Neutrino Observatory, honoured with the 2026 Physics Nobel, detects:
questions.e: Francis Halzen conceptualised and led IceCube; announced 6 Oct 2026.

questions.subject: Science
questions.q: Kagan and Soai's 2026 Chemistry Nobel recognised work on:
o: Non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis
questions.e: Announced 7 Oct 2026 by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The RBI's 63rd MPC meeting (5–7 Oct 2026) was chaired by:
questions.e: Repo raised 25 bps to 5.50%; stance changed to Calibrated Tightening.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: On 6 October 2026, BCCI appointed whom as India's women's white-ball captain?
questions.e: After Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down across all formats.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The Indian Air Force was established in:
questions.e: IAF Day is observed on 8 October every year.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: Ravindra Jadeja scored his 16th first-class century on 12 October 2026 against:
questions.e: 102 off 209 balls for Saurashtra vs Chhattisgarh at Rajkot in the Ranji Trophy 2026-27 opener; a 205-run stand with Prerak Mankad (129) took Saurashtra to 392.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: Anmol Kharb won the Türkiye International Challenge in October 2026 in:
questions.e: She beat compatriot Aakarshi Kashyap 21-11, 21-14 on 11 October 2026 — her third international senior title.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: India defeated West Indies by 14 runs in the 3rd T20I at Indore on 12 October 2026. The series now stands at:
questions.e: Abhishek Sharma smashed 69 off 30 balls as India posted 223 in the five-match T20I series.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: SAREX-2026, the 12th National Maritime Search & Rescue Exercise (7–8 Oct 2026), was conducted off:
questions.e: By the Indian Coast Guard with 32 observers from 30 countries; the scenario combined a 228-person aircraft ditching with a collision with container vessel MV Zumba.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.q: How many candidates were shortlisted for PET/PST in the SSC GD Constable 2026 result declared on 12 October 2026?
questions.e: The SSC GD Constable 2026 result was declared on 12 October 2026: 1,97,033 candidates were shortlisted for PET/PST out of 21,56,776 who appeared in the CBT (27 April–30 May 2026). Of these, 15,782 are female and 1,81,251 male, plus 375 additional male candidates for SSF.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.q: How many candidates were provisionally recommended in the SSC CHSL 2025 final result declared on 7 October 2026?
questions.e: The SSC declared the CHSL 2025 final result on 7 October 2026, provisionally recommending 3,515 candidates against 3,522 reported vacancies for LDC, JSA and DEO posts — after the first round of tentative allocation (17 August) and sliding/identity verification (1–3 September).

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: After the RBI’s 7 October 2026 policy, the SDF and MSF rates stand at:
questions.e: The RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50% on 7 October 2026, with the SDF at 5.25% and the MSF/Bank Rate at 5.75% — the corridor around the policy rate.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.q: What is the next stage for candidates shortlisted in the SSC GD Constable 2026 result?
questions.e: The SSC GD Constable 2026 CBT was held from 27 April to 30 May 2026, with 21,56,776 candidates appearing. The result (12 October 2026) shortlists candidates for the next stage — PET/PST.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: By what vote did the MPC change its stance to ‘calibrated tightening’ in October 2026?
questions.e: The MPC changed the stance from neutral to ‘calibrated tightening’ by a 4–2 majority on 7 October 2026 (the repo-rate hike itself was unanimous). This signals rate cuts are off the table in the near term.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: On 12 October 2026, President Droupadi Murmu appointed Braj Mohan Ram as the Governor of which state?
questions.e: Braj Mohan Ram was appointed Governor of Odisha. In the same 12 October 2026 reshuffle: Dr Sudha Yadav went to Karnataka, Dr Dhal Singh Bisen to Uttarakhand, Dushyant Gautam to Sikkim, Om Prakash Mathur was transferred from Sikkim to Kerala, and Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar was appointed Governor of Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: On 13 October 2026 the Supreme Court issued notice on a PIL challenging the blanket immunity granted to the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners under which provision?
o: Section 16 of the CEC and other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023
Section 14 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951
Section 11 of the Election Commission (Conditions of Service) Act, 1991
questions.e: The PIL challenges blanket immunity under Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. Notice was issued to the Centre and the ECI on 13 October 2026.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: On 13 October 2026, the Madras High Court upheld the Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker's decision accepting the resignations of how many AIADMK MLAs?
questions.e: The Court held the resignations of the six AIADMK MLAs were genuine and directed the Speaker to complete the disqualification proceedings against them within two months.

questions.subject: Science & Tech
questions.q: SpaceX's CRS-35 mission, launched on 13 October 2026, carried more than how much cargo to the International Space Station?
questions.e: The Falcon 9 lifted off from Space Launch Complex 40, Cape Canaveral, at 6:33 a.m. EDT on 13 October 2026 carrying the Cargo Dragon with more than 6,300 pounds (about 2,860 kg) of supplies and experiments, including the final pair of Redwire Roll-Out Solar Arrays.

questions.subject: Science & Tech
questions.q: Apple's first smart home hub, HomeView, announced on 13 October 2026, can recognise up to how many individual faces?
questions.e: HomeView, announced at Apple's 'Welcome Home' event on 13 October 2026, recognises up to six individuals and shows each a personalised display. It ships with Siri AI and the Apple Home Collection built with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric.

questions.subject: Education
questions.q: In the UGC NET re-examination results (English, Commerce, Sociology) declared in 2026, how many candidates qualified for the Junior Research Fellowship?
questions.e: 824 candidates qualified for JRF; 11,610 for Assistant Professor and 23,154 for PhD admission. The re-test was held on 9-10 September 2026 at 454 centres in 272 cities, with 1,96,491 registered and 1,20,355 appearing.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.q: What is the repo rate after the RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee meeting of 7 October 2026?
questions.e: The MPC raised the repo rate by 25 basis points from 5.25% to 5.50% on 7 October 2026, the first hike since February 2023.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.q: Who became the Governor of Karnataka in October 2026?
questions.e: Dr Sudha Yadav was appointed Governor of Karnataka on 12 October 2026, succeeding Thawar Chand Gehlot.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.q: Which Union Territory became India’s first 100% literate UT under ULLAS in October 2026?
questions.e: Lakshadweep was declared India’s first 100% literate Union Territory under ULLAS (Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.q: Who won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences?
questions.e: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford won the 2026 Economics Nobel “for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation”.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.q: The October 2026 IDBI Bank strategic sale to Fairfax is valued at:
questions.e: The Union Cabinet approved the IDBI Bank–Fairfax deal at ₹52,878 crore on 14 October 2026 — the largest-ever FDI in India’s financial sector.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Nobel Economics 2026: Hall & Woodford
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences went to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford — announced 12 Oct 2026 by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Bank of India: programmable Digital Rupee
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Bank of India launched user-level programmable CBDC auto-issuance on 29 Sep 2026 — scheduled, purpose-bound Digital Rupee transfers; developed by Montran India.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Diesel/ATF export levies cut from 1 Oct
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Diesel export levy ₹20→₹16/L and ATF ₹15→₹10.50/L from 1 Oct 2026; petrol levy unchanged at ₹0.50/L (Central Excise Notifications 52/2026, 53/2026 dated 30 Sep).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India beat West Indies by 14 runs
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — India won the T20I at Holkar Stadium, Indore, on 11 Oct 2026 by 14 runs — India 223/10 (Abhishek Sharma 69 off 30) beat West Indies 209/7.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: HDFC Bank: Anup Bagchi MD & CEO from 27 Oct
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Anup Bagchi takes charge as HDFC Bank's MD & CEO from 27 Oct 2026 — the bank's first external appointee to the role.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: 3rd Sagarmanthan oceans dialogue held
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The 3rd Sagarmanthan: The Great Oceans Dialogue was held 7–9 Oct 2026 in New Delhi on ‘Blue Geographies, New Aspirations: Trade, Technology, and Trust at Sea’ — 1,200 participants from ~75 countries; organised by ORF and the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI hikes repo rate to 5.50%
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — RBI's MPC raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% on 7 Oct 2026 — first hike since Feb 2023, unanimous; stance 'calibrated tightening'; FY27 GDP 7.1%, CPI 5.2% (RBI).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Ashutosh Dixit: 29th Air Chief from 31 Oct
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit takes charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on 31 Oct 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh (PIB).

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Three HC CJs elevated to Supreme Court
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — On 5 Oct 2026 the President appointed Justices Sunita Agarwal (Gujarat CJ), Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya (Delhi CJ) and Aparesh Kumar Singh (Telangana CJ) as Supreme Court judges under Article 124(2).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Nobel Prizes 2026: Physics & Chemistry
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Physics: Francis Halzen (IceCube neutrino observatory); Chemistry: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai; Medicine (5 Oct): Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel (optogenetics).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: ITLA approved by Cabinet
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The Union Cabinet approved the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority as an SPV on 6 Oct 2026 — apex body for integrated transport planning (PIB).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: New India Assurance gets new CMD
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Lavanya R Mundayur appointed CMD of New India Assurance (order 30 Sep 2026; tenure till 31 May 2029); earlier CMD of AICIL.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: INS Trishul at Plymouth for Konkan-2026
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — INS Trishul reached Plymouth, UK, for bilateral Exercise Konkan-2026 with the Royal Navy (PIB, 11 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: INS Sahyadri at Vladivostok for Indra-2026
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — INS Sahyadri reached Vladivostok, Russia, for bilateral Exercise Indra-2026 (PIB, 11 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Navy to induct ASW vessel ‘Mangrole’
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — The Indian Navy will induct the indigenous anti-submarine warfare vessel ‘Mangrole’ (PIB, 10 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Chennai: ₹13,000 cr projects on 11 Oct
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — PM Modi launches Chennai projects worth over ₹13,000 crore on 11 Oct; the Chennai Metro Phase II Poonamallee–Vadapalani stretch (~₹4,900 crore) includes a 3.7-km double-decker structure (PMO, 10 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave concludes
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — The 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave (KEC 2026) concluded in New Delhi on the theme ‘Resilience in an Era of Transformation’ (PIB, 11 Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: UPI-MDR from 15 Oct: 0.4% above ₹2,000
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — From 15 Oct 2026, specified UPI merchant payments above ₹2,000 carry 0.4% MDR (capped at ₹300); railways, telecom, insurance and fuel get a flat ₹5; person-to-person transfers stay free.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Nobel Chemistry 2026: Kagan & Soai
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — Henri B. Kagan (95, France) and Kenso Soai (76, Japan) won the Chemistry Nobel 'for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis'.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel Literature 2026: Anne Carson
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — Canadian writer Anne Carson, 76, won the Literature Nobel 'for her bold and inventive oeuvre' — the 19th woman and second Canadian laureate.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Bihar: 14 lakh voters added
capsules.body: Oct 2026 — Nearly 14 lakh voters were added to Bihar's rolls after SIR (18.7 lakh Form-6 applications); the electorate is now 7.55 crore.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Bihar Congress agitation
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — Phased voter-rights agitation: block marches 10–20 Oct, 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' chaupals 25 Oct–25 Nov, Delhi Chalo on Constitution Day; demands: CEC's resignation and SIR rollback.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: IND vs WI 3rd T20I today
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — India vs West Indies 3rd T20I today at Holkar Stadium, Indore (7 PM IST); WI chased 250 in the 2nd T20I — Hope 102* off 45, Rutherford 84 off 37.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: GST: arrest powers scrapped
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — The 57th GST Council scrapped arrest powers under GST and raised the prosecution threshold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: GST: penalty Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — The general penalty under GST was cut from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000; refund acknowledgement cut from 15 to 10 days.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: GST: 1.70 cr taxpayers
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — GST taxpayers rose from ~60 lakh (2017) to 1.70 crore (Sept 2026); Apr–Sep 2026 collections Rs 12.46 lakh crore (+11.6% YoY).

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Delhi protest: 15,000+ detained
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — The CJP's Jantar Mantar protest (CEC resignation + SIR rollback demand) saw 23,000+ security personnel, 45 metro stations shut and 15,000+ detained.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: CEC Gyanesh Kumar in spotlight
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — The protest demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI dollar window for oil firms
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — The RBI opened a special dollar window for Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL (from 12 Oct) and cut the rupee exchange-traded derivative limit from $100 million to $5 million.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel Peace 2026: Navi Pillay
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay, 85, won the Nobel Peace Prize 'for her efforts to promote peace and international law'. She is of Indian Tamil origin and served as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (2008–14).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Nobel Physics 2026: Francis Halzen
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Francis Halzen won the Physics Nobel for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Bihar MLC polls on 23 Oct
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — Biennial polls for 8 Bihar Legislative Council seats (4 Graduates' + 4 Teachers') on 23 October 2026; 164 candidates; counting on 27 October.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI: CRR 99% daily from 16 Oct
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — Minimum daily CRR maintenance rises from 90% to 99% of the prescribed requirement from the fortnight beginning 16 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel Literature: Anne Carson
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature (announced 8 Oct) was awarded to Canadian author Anne Carson, ‘for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature.’

capsules.subject: Persons
capsules.title: Nana Patekar (1951–2026)
