capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — Veteran actor Nana Patekar (born Vishwanath Patekar, 1 Jan 1951) died of cardiac arrest at his Dona Paula, Goa residence on 8 Oct, aged 75 — declared dead at 5:20 am after doctors attempted CPR for ~45 minutes. A recipient of three National Film Awards (Parinda, Agni Sakshi, Krantiveer) and the Padma Shri (2013), he was cremated with full state honours at his Donje farmhouse in Pune.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Sensex: -1,177 to 71,461
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The Sensex crashed 1,177 points to close at 71,461 and the Nifty fell 371 points to 22,231 (an 18-month low) on 8 Oct, wiping out ~₹10 lakh crore of investor wealth. Triggers: the RBI hiked the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% (its first hike in nearly four years) and shifted its stance to ‘calibrated tightening’, Brent crude crossed $104/barrel, and FIIs sold ₹6,121 crore of equities.

capsules.subject: Days
capsules.title: 9 Oct: World Post Day
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — World Post Day is observed on 9 October (it is also World Egg Day).

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: AP drought: 53.4% deficit
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — Andhra Pradesh has declared drought in 388 of its 688 mandals across 21 of 26 districts (283 severe, 105 moderate) for Kharif 2026, after a 53.4% rainfall deficit — 197.6 mm against a normal 424.3 mm (June–August) — amplified by prevailing El Niño conditions. The 1 Oct order follows the Manual for Drought Management, 2016.

capsules.subject: Sci-Tech
capsules.title: Jio: 1,600 satellites
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — Reliance Jio unveiled ‘Sovereign Satellite Connectivity’ at India Mobile Congress 2026 (10th edition, inaugurated by PM Modi on 8 Oct; theme ‘Scale Without Boundaries’): a proposed constellation of ~1,600 low-earth-orbit satellites with 23 ground stations in India, targeting 100% land-and-maritime coverage reaching 600,000+ villages, plus direct-to-device calling for rural areas.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Rahul, Priyanka detained: EC march
capsules.body: 7 Oct 2026 — Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were detained by Delhi Police on Tuesday evening after an hours-long sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan during the INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR (Special Intensive Revision) of electoral rolls.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Next CAS: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit
capsules.body: 7 Oct 2026 — The government has named Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit as the next Chief of the Air Staff, effective 31 October.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: BrahMos: ₹661.5 cr Navy deal
capsules.body: 7 Oct 2026 — The Defence Ministry signed a ₹661.50 crore contract for BrahMos fire-control systems and launchers for Indian Navy ships.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: GST H1 FY27: +11.6%
capsules.body: 7 Oct 2026 — GST collections in the first half of FY27 rose 11.6%, driven by imports and manufacturing growth, with September collections strong.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Titan Q2: +25% YoY
capsules.body: 7 Oct 2026 — Titan's consumer businesses grew 25% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, driven by strong growth in jewellery, watches and eyewear.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Nobel Chemistry: announced today
capsules.body: 7 Oct 2026 — The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry will be announced today at 3:15 PM IST by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. The physics prize went to Francis Halzen (IceCube Neutrino Observatory) on 6 Oct and the medicine prize to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel (optogenetics) on 5 Oct; literature follows on 8 Oct, peace on 9 Oct and economics on 12 Oct.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Nobel Physics: IceCube
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics “for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin”, announced by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. IceCube is a cubic-kilometre neutrino detector frozen into the Antarctic ice at the South Pole; its optical sensors catch the faint flashes of rare high-energy neutrinos arriving from deep space. The chemistry prize follows on 7 Oct, literature on 8 Oct, peace on 9 Oct and economics on 12 Oct.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: 3 new SC judges sworn in
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Justices Sunita Agarwal (Gujarat HC Chief Justice), Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya (Delhi HC Chief Justice) and Aparesh Kumar Singh (Telangana HC Chief Justice) were sworn in as Supreme Court judges at a rare 3:30 PM ceremony, with CJI Surya Kant administering the oath. The Centre had notified the appointments on 5 Oct after the collegium's 28 September recommendation. Working strength rises from 34 to 37 — one short of the sanctioned 38, raised from 34 by the Supreme Court Amendment Act, 2026. Justice Agarwal becomes the third woman judge, alongside Justices B.V. Nagarathna and Venkita Subramani Mohana.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Harmanpreet steps down
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down as captain of the Indian women's cricket team across all formats with immediate effect, ending a decade-long leadership stint. The 37-year-old confirmed the decision on 6 October 2026; she will, however, continue to play for India.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: BoB: pension fund entry
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Bank of Baroda (BoB) has become the second public sector bank in India to enter the pension fund business, receiving a Certificate of Appointment as Sponsor of a Pension Fund from the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA). The approval was granted under Section 27 of the PFRDA Act, 2013.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Wildlife Week theme
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — The 72nd National Wildlife Week is being observed across India from 2 to 8 October 2026, on the theme “Connecting Habitats, Thriving Wildlife” — stressing habitat connectivity so wild animals can move safely between forests, grasslands and other ecosystems. Roots: the Indian Board for Wildlife was constituted in 1952; the observance became week-long in 1957. Separately, World Cerebral Palsy Day 2026 is observed on 6 October.

capsules.subject: Culture
capsules.title: Singeetham passes away
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Veteran Indian filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao passed away in October 2026 at the age of 94 in a hospital in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Born on 21 September 1931 in Gudur, Andhra Pradesh, he was known for his experimental storytelling and contributions to Indian cinema across several languages.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: CJI: SC approved no Form 6 changes
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — CJI Surya Kant said the Supreme Court did not approve "any" modifications to Form 6, the form voters fill to register, as a three-judge bench headed by him heard petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Separately, the Court issued notices to the Election Commission and the Centre, observing that decisions taken without unanimity or majority could be annulled, amid the Form 6 controversy.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Six by-elections vote today
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Voting is underway today in six by-elections: Nandigram and Rejinagar (West Bengal), Madurantakam and Dharapuram (Tamil Nadu), Thattanchavady (Puducherry) and the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat (Assam). All six fell vacant after winners of the April 2026 general and assembly elections resigned one of two seats they had contested.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: India–Switzerland migration pact signed
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — India and Switzerland on 5 Oct signed a migration and mobility partnership pact and agreed to expand Swiss market access for Indian exports, after talks between PM Narendra Modi and Swiss President Guy Parmelin in New Delhi. The two sides also agreed to deepen cooperation in nuclear energy, defence and critical technologies.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: IOAA: India wins 4 gold, 1 silver
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — India won four gold medals and one silver at the 19th International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics (IOAA), one of the country's strongest showings at the event.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: IndiGo hikes fuel surcharge after ATF rise
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — IndiGo has raised fuel surcharges on domestic and international tickets after another hike in aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices, adding to rising air-travel costs.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Delhi: drizzle today; AQI 238 at Alipur
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Delhi is likely to see very light rain or drizzle today (IMD), with the maximum at 34–36°C and minimum 22–24°C. At 5 AM the AQI stood at 238 (poor) at Alipur and 229 (poor) at Vivek Vihar, while Anand Vihar (169), Ashok Vihar (147) and Aya Nagar (146) were moderate.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Nobel 2026: optogenetics wins medicine prize
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — Karl Deisseroth (54, American), Peter Hegemann (71, German) and Georg Nagel (73, German) won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine “for discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics”, announced by the Nobel Assembly at Sweden's Karolinska Institute. Optogenetics lets scientists switch individual nerve cells in a living brain on or off with light; the method is used in labs worldwide to reveal neural circuits behind memory, feelings and behaviour, and is being explored to restore sight. Hegemann and Nagel discovered the light-sensitive channelrhodopsin protein in the alga Chlamydomonas; Deisseroth (Stanford) showed in 2005 that it can control nerve cells. The 12-million-Swedish-crown prize (about $1.2 million) is shared; the physics, chemistry, literature, peace and economics prizes follow this week.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Cricket gold: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — India defended their Asian Games men's cricket gold on 3 Oct, beating Pakistan by 19 runs in the final at Nisshin (India 211/6, Pakistan 192/6). Abhishek Sharma's 61 off 28 and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51 off 22 powered India; Hasan Nawaz's 51-ball 96 kept Pakistan in the hunt. Shreyas Iyer won the toss and chose to bat. It was the first India–Pakistan clash at the Asian Games, and the two sides avoided the customary handshakes. The gold completes a cricket double — India's women beat Sri Lanka in the final on 22 September — and Sri Lanka took bronze, beating Bangladesh by 63 runs.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI MPC: hike decision due 7 October
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — The RBI's six-member Monetary Policy Committee began its three-day meeting today; the repo-rate decision is due on 7 October. Markets widely expect a 25 bps hike to 5.50% — which would be the first increase since February 2023, when the rate was raised to 6.50%. The repo rate has sat at 5.25% through four consecutive reviews after cumulative 125 bps cuts in 2025. Drivers: August CPI at 4.82% (third straight month above the 4% target), Brent crude near $101 a barrel, and the US Fed's recent hike. A 25 bps rise could push floating home-loan rates from 8.5% to 8.75%, adding about ₹795 a month to a ₹50 lakh, 20-year EMI.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: Delhi AQI: 187, highest in 83 days
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — Delhi's air quality hit an 83-day high of 187 ('moderate') on 4 Oct and eased to 183 on 5 Oct, per the CPCB; the last higher reading was 246 on 13 July. Sixteen monitoring stations recorded 'poor' air (Mundka 273, Narela 257), and NCR cities Noida (281), Ghaziabad (248) and Faridabad (224) slipped into 'poor' too. If the AQI crosses 200, GRAP Stage 1 kicks in. CPCB bands: 0–50 good, 51–100 satisfactory, 101–200 moderate, 201–300 poor, 301–400 very poor, 401–500 severe. The IARI recorded 203 stubble-burning incidents across Punjab, UP and MP between 15 September and 3 October; Delhi saw its most polluted October start in four years.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Handshakes avoided in historic final
capsules.body: The 3 Oct final was the first India–Pakistan clash at the Asian Games. The match passed off without drama but the sides avoided the customary handshakes — a detail examiners love for sports-GK questions.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Prize calendar: what follows medicine
capsules.body: After medicine (5 Oct): physics (6 Oct), chemistry (7 Oct), then literature, peace and economics. The order itself is a standard static-GK question.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Bihar: 7 engineers suspended over Gandak floods
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — The Bihar government has suspended seven engineers and ordered departmental proceedings against Muzaffarpur chief engineer Kumar Manoj Gupta for alleged negligence in handling the recent floods, the Water Resources Department said on 4 Oct. The suspended officials include Saran executive engineer Santosh Kumar Prabhakar and Gopalganj executive engineer Md Sajid Iqbal. The Gandak is receding: at Rewaghat in Saran it has fallen 177 cm from its record high to 50 cm below the danger mark, while at Lalganj in Vaishali it has dropped 130 cm but remains 52 cm above the danger mark.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: UPSC turns 100: 45-fold growth since 1976
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — The Union Public Service Commission completed 100 years on 1 Oct 2026: at Bharat Mandapam the Prime Minister released a commemorative stamp, a coin and a compilation of 100 judgments shaping the commission's work; the number of exam-takers has grown 45-fold since 1976, and three of the four chairpersons appointed since 2014 have been women.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: OPEC+ holds Nov quotas; Brent $102.25
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — OPEC+ agreed on 4 Oct to keep oil production quotas steady for November; Brent crude closed Friday at $102.25 a barrel in New York, as the G7's release of 100 million barrels from strategic reserves (including diesel) counters record prices blamed on the Iran and Ukraine wars.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games 2026 officially closed
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 were officially declared closed on 4 Oct by OCA President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani; India finished fourth with 85 medals — 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.

capsules.subject: International
capsules.title: Brazil votes: Lula vs Flávio Bolsonaro
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — Brazil votes today in a presidential election pitting 80-year-old leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva against far-right rival Flavio Bolsonaro, son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro (serving a 27-year sentence over a failed-coup plot); polls show Lula with a slender lead.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Delhi: Rs 1,789.52 cr traffic system
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — The Union Cabinet has approved a Rs 1,789.52-crore intelligent traffic management system for Delhi: 42 corridors, 1,092 adaptive signal points and 1,029 enforcement points, to be built in three phases over 24 months and operated for five years after that.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Bhadohi renamed Sant Ravidas Nagar Bhadohi
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — UP CM Yogi Adityanath renamed Bhadohi district as 'Sant Ravidas Nagar Bhadohi', honouring the medieval saint; the announcement came at a programme launching 112 development projects worth over ₹1,340 crore. Bhadohi is famous for its carpet industry.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Deepwater gas ceiling: $9.89/MMBtu
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — The government raised the ceiling price of natural gas from deepwater, ultra-deepwater and HPHT fields to $9.89/MMBtu (from $8.90) for 1 Oct 2026–31 Mar 2027, per a PPAC notification — relief for producers like Reliance-BP's KG-D6. The ceiling for ONGC/OIL nomination fields stays at $7/MMBtu; the October APM price was notified at $11.22/MMBtu.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Rabi MSP: mustard +₹413, lentil +₹390
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — The Cabinet fixed rabi MSP for 2026-27: mustard +₹413/quintal and lentil (masur) +₹390/quintal — the two biggest hikes — and wheat +₹25/quintal (<1%), signalling a push for oilseeds and pulses. IMD closed the 2026 monsoon at 759.4 mm — 87% of the long-period average — with 17 of 36 subdivisions deficient under a strong El Niño.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: India's first 5.56-km QKD link
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — India demonstrated its first 5.56-km free-space Quantum Key Distribution link — using quantum states of photons to share encryption keys with theoretically unbreakable security, a milestone for secure communication.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: 153rd IPU Assembly in Tanzania
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — An Indian parliamentary delegation led by Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh left for Tanzania for the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (5–9 Oct). The IPU, founded in 1889 and headquartered in Geneva, is the global organisation of national parliaments.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Leprosy: 3,832 children; 2027 target
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — 3,832 children were diagnosed with leprosy in India, reported as the country works toward interrupting leprosy transmission by 2027 under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme. Leprosy (Hansen's disease) is caused by Mycobacterium leprae and is curable with multidrug therapy (dapsone, rifampicin, clofazimine).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India 4th at Asian Games: 85 medals
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — India finished 4th at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 with 85 medals: 21 gold, 27 silver, 37 bronze. China topped with 341 medals (169 gold), hosts Japan were second with 269 (83 gold), South Korea third with 150 (39 gold). India matched Uzbekistan on 21 golds but stayed ahead on silvers. The Games close today with the closing ceremony at Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium (2:30–4 PM IST).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Men's hockey 5-1 vs Malaysia: LA28 quota
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — India thrashed Malaysia 5-1 in the Asian Games men's hockey final on 3 Oct: captain Harmanpreet Singh scored twice (including a 12th-minute drag-flick), Hardik Singh converted a penalty stroke, and Shilanand Lakra bagged one; Malaysia's Shello Silverius replied. India's 21st gold sealed a direct LA 2028 Olympic quota and — with the women's 1-0 win over China on 2 Oct — the first-ever Asian Games where BOTH Indian teams took hockey gold.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Neeru Dhanda: flag bearer, 3 medals
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — Trap shooter Neeru Dhanda, 27, carries the Tricolour as India's flag bearer at today's closing ceremony. She won three medals: women's trap individual gold with 28 hits (an Asian record, topping qualification with 118 — the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games trap gold), trap mixed-team gold with Kynan Chenai (34 hits, breaking the Asian record of 33), and women's team trap silver with Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer (combined 328). She also won ISSF World Cup gold at Lonato earlier this year.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Closing ceremony today, 2:30–4 PM IST
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — The 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games close TODAY: the closing ceremony is at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium between 2:30 PM and 4 PM IST, with double-gold trap shooter Neeru Dhanda leading the Indian contingent as flag bearer.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Antim Panghal: 53kg wrestling silver
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — Wrestler Antim Panghal took silver in the women's 53kg freestyle on 3 Oct, losing 9-1 to Japan's Moe Kiyooka in the final — India's 27th silver of the Games, a crucial one in the race with Uzbekistan for 4th place in the medal table.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: MPC 5–7 Oct: 25 bps hike expected
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — The RBI's six-member Monetary Policy Committee meets 5–7 October (decision on 7 Oct): 8 of 10 economists in a Business Standard poll expect the first rate hike since February 2023 — 25 basis points, taking the repo rate from 5.25% to 5.50%. The RBI has held the repo unchanged for four straight reviews after cutting a cumulative 125 bps in 2025.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Ind beat Pak by 19 runs in Asian Games cricket final
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the Asian Games 2026 men's cricket final at Nisshin: India 211/6 (Abhishek Sharma 61 off 28, incl. a 20-ball fifty; Tilak Varma 51* off 22) beat Pakistan 192/6 (Hasan Nawaz 96 off 51). India's second consecutive Asian Games gold, completing a cricket double with the women's gold.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Pranavi Urs: first Indian woman with Asian Games golf gold
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — Pranavi Sharath Urs (23, Mysuru) won India's first-ever Asian Games women's individual golf gold: 15-under 265 at Kasugai Country Club East; she entered the final round with a 3-stroke lead, survived a triple bogey on the 3rd, and closed with an even-par 70; she also helped India to the women's team silver.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Kumkum Mohod: recurve gold via shoot-off, LA28 quota
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — Kumkum Anil Mohod, 17, won India's first Asian Games women's recurve individual archery gold: she beat South Korea's Oh Yejin 6-5 in a one-arrow shoot-off (10 vs 8) after a 5-5 tie, and secured India an individual quota place for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics (the quota belongs to the country, not the athlete).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Cabinet clears GEC-III: ₹1.86 lakh crore
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — The Union Cabinet (30 Sep) approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III: a ₹1,86,405-crore scheme (₹1,36,378 cr for intra-state transmission + ₹50,000 cr for 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage) to evacuate up to 135 GW of renewable energy, with ₹54,082 crore of central support; completion targeted by FY 2032-33.

capsules.subject: Geography
capsules.title: Hingoli earthquake: magnitude 4.5 at 9:43 am
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — An earthquake of magnitude 4.5 hit Hingoli, Maharashtra, at about 9:43 am (National Center for Seismology); tremors of magnitude 3.4 in Myanmar and 3.6 in Tibet were also reported today.

capsules.subject: Infrastructure
capsules.title: Katra–Banihal: 100 kmph; Chenab Bridge 359 m
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — Train speeds on the Katra–Banihal section in Jammu & Kashmir have been raised to up to 100 kmph; the route includes the Chenab Bridge, the world's highest railway arch bridge, standing about 359 metres above the Chenab river.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Hockey gold after 44 years
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — India's women beat China 1-0 in the Asian Games hockey final at Kakamigahara on 2 Oct: Lalremsiami's 10th-minute reverse-stick goal on her 200th cap, and Savita Punia's penalty-stroke save (vs Zhang Ying, 2nd quarter), ended a 44-year wait — India's second women's hockey gold (first: 1982) and a direct LA 2028 Olympic quota (India missed Paris 2024). Hockey India: ₹11 lakh per player, ₹5.5 lakh per support staff. Japan beat South Korea 4-2 in a shootout for bronze.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Archery: first women's recurve team gold
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — India's women's recurve team (Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma, 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod) beat South Korea 5-3 for India's first-ever Asian Games women's recurve team gold; the men's recurve trio (Dhiraj Bommadevara, Neeraj Chauhan, Yashdeep Bhoge) took silver, and Dhiraj+Kumkum added mixed-team silver.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Boxing treble on 2 Oct
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — India's richest Asian Games boxing day: three golds — Lovlina Borgohain (women's 75kg, 5-0 vs China's Bao Ziyi), Parveen Hooda (women's 65kg, 3-2 vs Chinese Taipei's Chen Nien-chin; third Indian woman after Mary Kom and Lovlina), Ankush Panghal (men's 80kg, 4-0 vs South Korea's Kim Minseong).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Sujeet's 10–9 wrestling comeback
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — Sujeet Kalkal won Asian Games men's 65kg freestyle gold, storming back from 2-9 down to beat Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev 10-9 with a takedown 11 seconds from time; he beat an Olympic champion en route. (Day 12: Nitesh Siwach took wrestling silver.)

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: GST: ₹2.04 lakh crore
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — September gross GST collections hit ₹2.04 lakh crore, up 14.7% year-on-year, on steady economic activity and pre-festive inventory build-up.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: NVS-03: 15–20 Oct window
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — ISRO targets 15-20 October 2026 for NVS-03 (IRNSS-1L) aboard GSLV-F18 from Sriharikota's Second Launch Pad: the ~2,232-kg satellite restores NavIC to four working satellites (IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I, NVS-01) with L1/L5/S and C-band ranging payloads and rubidium atomic clocks; NVS-04 and NVS-05 are in advanced development; PSLV stays on hold after two failures.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Gandhi Jayanti 2026: 157th birth anniversary
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — India marks the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi (born 2 Oct 1869): President Droupadi Murmu attended the Sarva-Dharma Prarthana at Rajghat; PM Modi urged every Indian to buy at least one Khadi product and say 'This is Swadeshi!'; 2 October is also the International Day of Non-Violence (UN resolution, 2007).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: NVS-03: NavIC's third second-gen satellite
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — ISRO plans to launch NVS-03, the third of five second-generation NavIC navigation satellites, in mid-October 2026 aboard a GSLV Mk II from Sriharikota; the ~2,250-kg satellite will restore the constellation to four working satellites (with IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I, NVS-01) and broadcasts in the L1, L5 and S bands.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: SC quashes Sambhal NSA detention
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court quashed the NSA detention of Sambhal-violence accused Mulla Afroz (29 Sep 2026), holding a custodial confession alone cannot ground preventive detention, and imposed a ₹10 lakh cost on the Uttar Pradesh government (Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu).

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: NCERT's new Class 9 books bring tax to class
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — NCERT released two more Class 9 textbooks: 'Ganita Manjari – Part 2' (Maths, on sale from 21 Sep) and 'Understanding Society: India & Beyond – Part 2' (Social Science, from 30 Sep); the SST book's Chapter 5 'Managing Your Personal Finances' teaches income-tax slab calculations, and Chapter 4 presents NEP 2020 as a model of consultative policymaking.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Savitha Shri: India's only individual chess gold
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — 19-year-old Savitha Shri Baskar of Chennai was India's only individual gold medallist at the Chess Olympiad 2026 in Samarkand, anchoring the women's team's bronze with 8 wins from 9 games, including a decisive win over China's Zhai Mo.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games cricket final: India vs Pakistan 3 Oct
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — India face Pakistan in the Asian Games 2026 men's cricket final on 3 October at Korogi Sports Park, Nisshin — the first-ever India-Pakistan clash at the Asian Games; India, the defending champions (Hangzhou 2022), stormed in with a 124-run semifinal win over Sri Lanka (169/7; Ishan Kishan 80* off 46; Sri Lanka 45 all out).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games hockey: India 4-3 Pakistan
capsules.body: On 1 October 2026 defending champions India beat Pakistan 4-3 in the men's hockey semifinal at the Asian Games 2026 to reach the final.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games cricket: India into final vs Pakistan
capsules.body: India beat Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the men's cricket semifinal on 1 October 2026; the gold-medal match against Pakistan is on 3 October.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: FASTag Annual Pass crosses 1 crore
capsules.body: FASTag Annual Pass issuances crossed one crore on 1 October 2026 since the August 2025 launch; the ₹3,075 pass gives one-year validity or 200 toll crossings across about 1,150 plazas.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: NHAI to inspect 17 highway projects
capsules.body: NHAI ordered special quality inspections of 17 under-construction National Highway projects where bid values were more than 15% below the estimated project cost, announced 1 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Agriculture
capsules.title: Khet Bachao Abhiyan from 22 October
capsules.body: The Centre announced the Khet Bachao Abhiyan (22 October–30 November 2026) focused on soil health and balanced fertiliser use, alongside over ₹1,200 crore sanctioned under PM-RKVY to 10 states.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Mumbai property registrations hit 14-year high
capsules.body: Mumbai recorded 12,622 property registrations in September 2026, up 5% year-on-year — the highest September total in over 14 years, per Knight Frank India analysis reported 1 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: SSC CGL Tier 1 admit cards released in phases
capsules.body: SSC released the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 admit cards in phases from 27 September 2026, starting with candidates appearing on 30 September; the Tier 1 computer-based exam runs 30 September to 30 October 2026 (official notice F.No. HQ-EC033/7/2025-EC). Hall tickets are downloadable from ssc.gov.in via candidate login using the registration number and password.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: SSC GD Constable 2027: notice expected 30 Sep
capsules.body: As per the SSC 2026-27 examination calendar, the Constable (GD) 2027 notification is expected on 30 September 2026 with the application window open into October; the computer-based exam is scheduled for January-March 2027. Vacancy figures for the 2027 cycle had not been published yet.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: SSC CHSL 2026: apply before 7 October
capsules.body: SSC CHSL 2026 applications (notified 7 September 2026 for about 2,536 LDC/JSA and DEO posts) close on 7 October 2026 at 11 pm; the last date for fee payment is 8 October and the correction window runs 14-16 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Selection Post Phase-XIV CBE held 16-26 Sep
capsules.body: SSC conducted the Selection Posts Phase-XIV 2026 computer-based exam from 16 to 26 September 2026. In a related notice the Commission integrated scribe registration with Aadhaar authentication, making fresh registration mandatory for candidates using the own-scribe facility.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: SSC CGL 2026: fixed sectional timing, new Tier 2 Paper-III
capsules.body: For SSC CGL 2026 the Commission introduced fixed sectional timing in both tiers and a new Paper-III in Tier 2 for Junior Statistical Officer posts. Tier 1 (30 Sep to 30 Oct 2026) carries 100 questions of 2 marks each (200 marks) in 60 minutes.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel Physics 2025
capsules.body: John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel Chemistry 2025
capsules.body: Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), porous materials used for gas storage and carbon capture.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel Medicine 2025
capsules.body: Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell and Shimon Sakaguchi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Medicine for discoveries on peripheral immune tolerance and regulatory T cells.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel Literature 2025
capsules.body: Hungarian writer László Krasznahorkai won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature for a visionary body of work that reaffirms the power of art amid apocalyptic terror.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel Peace 2025
capsules.body: Venezuela's María Corina Machado won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize for her struggle for democratic rights and a peaceful transition from dictatorship to democracy in Venezuela.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Nobel Economics 2025
capsules.body: Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt won the 2025 economics Nobel for work on innovation-led growth and the theory of creative destruction.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: 71st National Film Awards
capsules.body: Announced 1 August 2025 for 2023 cinema: 12th Fail won Best Feature Film; Shah Rukh Khan (Jawan) and Vikrant Massey (12th Fail) shared Best Actor; Rani Mukerji (Mrs Chatterjee vs Norway) won Best Actress.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Dadasaheb Phalke Award 2023
capsules.body: Veteran actor Mohanlal received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2023, presented at the 71st National Film Awards ceremony in 2025.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Booker Prize 2025
capsules.body: Hungarian-British writer David Szalay won the 2025 Booker Prize for his novel 'Flesh'.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Oscars 2025
capsules.body: At the 97th Academy Awards, 'Anora' won Best Picture; Adrien Brody (The Brutalist) won Best Actor and Mikey Madison (Anora) won Best Actress.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Padma Awards 2025
capsules.body: Announced on the eve of Republic Day 2025: 139 Padma awards in all — 7 Padma Vibhushan, 19 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Jnanpith Award 2024
capsules.body: Hindi writer Vinod Kumar Shukla received the 59th Jnanpith Award (for 2024), announced in 2025.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Grammy Awards 2025
capsules.body: Kendrick Lamar's 'Not Like Us' won both Record and Song of the Year; Beyoncé's 'Cowboy Carter' won Album of the Year at the 2025 Grammys.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Abel Prize 2025
capsules.body: Japanese mathematician Masaki Kashiwara won the 2025 Abel Prize for contributions to algebraic analysis and representation theory.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: National Sports Awards 2024
capsules.body: Announced January 2025: the Khel Ratna went to Manu Bhaker, D. Gukesh, Harmanpreet Singh and Praveen Kumar.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: International Booker 2025
capsules.body: 'Heart Lamp' by Banu Mushtaq, translated from Kannada by Deepa Bhasthi, won the 2025 International Booker Prize — the first short-story collection to win it.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Pritzker Prize 2025
capsules.body: Chinese architect Liu Jiakun won the 2025 Pritzker Architecture Prize.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Miss World 2025
capsules.body: Opal Suchata Chuangsri of Thailand won Miss World 2025 at the pageant held in Hyderabad, India.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: Pulitzer Prize 2025
capsules.body: Percival Everett's novel 'James' won the 2025 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

capsules.subject: Awards
capsules.title: 70th Filmfare Awards
capsules.body: 'Laapataa Ladies' dominated the 70th Filmfare Awards (held 2025), sweeping the major honours for 2024 Hindi cinema.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: T20 World Cup 2026
capsules.body: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs in the final at Ahmedabad on 8 March 2026 to win a record third T20 World Cup — the first team to successfully defend the title; Jasprit Bumrah was Player of the Match.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Champions Trophy 2025
capsules.body: India beat New Zealand by four wickets in the final at Dubai on 9 March 2025 to win a record third Champions Trophy; Rohit Sharma (76 off 83) was Player of the Match and Rachin Ravindra Player of the Tournament.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asia Cup 2025
capsules.body: India beat Pakistan by five wickets in the final at Dubai on 28 September 2025 to win a record ninth Asia Cup; Tilak Varma (69*) anchored the chase and Kuldeep Yadav took 4/30.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asia Cup trophy row
capsules.body: After winning the 2025 Asia Cup, India declined to accept the trophy from ACC chief Mohsin Naqvi — the first time champions left without lifting the trophy.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: IPL 2025
capsules.body: Royal Challengers Bengaluru beat Punjab Kings by six runs in the final at Ahmedabad to win their maiden IPL title; Krunal Pandya (2/17) was Player of the Match.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: WPL 2025
capsules.body: Mumbai Indians beat Delhi Capitals by eight runs in the final at Brabourne Stadium on 15 March 2025 to win their second WPL title; Harmanpreet Kaur was Player of the Match.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: WPL 2025 awards
capsules.body: Nat Sciver-Brunt was Player of the Tournament and Orange Cap winner in WPL 2025; Amelia Kerr won the Purple Cap for most wickets.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: FIDE Women's World Cup 2025
capsules.body: Divya Deshmukh beat Koneru Humpy 1.5-0.5 in the tiebreaks to win the 2025 FIDE Women's World Cup at Batumi, becoming a Grandmaster in the process.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Neeraj crosses 90m
capsules.body: Neeraj Chopra breached the 90-metre mark for the first time at the Doha Diamond League in May 2025, throwing 90.23 m.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
capsules.body: The 2026 FIFA World Cup, hosted by the USA, Canada and Mexico, is the first edition with 48 teams.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Winter Olympics 2026
capsules.body: The 2026 Winter Olympics were held at Milano Cortina, Italy, in February 2026.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games 2026
capsules.body: The 2026 Asian Games are scheduled at Nagoya, Japan; India won a record 107 medals at the previous edition in Hangzhou.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Commonwealth Games 2026
capsules.body: The 2026 Commonwealth Games are scheduled at Glasgow, Scotland, in a scaled-down format.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Test retirements 2025
capsules.body: Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma both announced retirement from Test cricket in May 2025.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy
capsules.body: India drew the five-Test series in England 2-2 in 2025, the first edition played for the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy (as reported).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Border-Gavaskar Trophy
capsules.body: Australia beat India 3-1 to regain the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in the 2024-25 series, decided at Sydney in January 2025.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: WTC Final 2025
capsules.body: South Africa beat Australia in the 2025 World Test Championship final at Lord's to win their first ICC title (as reported).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: U19 Women's T20 World Cup
capsules.body: India beat South Africa in the final at Kuala Lumpur to defend their ICC U19 Women's T20 World Cup title in 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Chhetri comeback
capsules.body: Sunil Chhetri reversed his 2024 international retirement and returned to the Indian football team in March 2025.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: ICC Awards 2024
capsules.body: Jasprit Bumrah won the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy as ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year 2024, and Smriti Mandhana won the ICC Women's ODI Cricketer of the Year 2024 (announced January 2025).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: National Games 2025
capsules.body: Uttarakhand hosted the 38th National Games in January-February 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Khelo India Youth Games 2025
capsules.body: Bihar hosted the Khelo India Youth Games 2025 in May 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Neeraj Chopra Classic
capsules.body: The inaugural Neeraj Chopra Classic javelin meet was held at Bengaluru in July 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Animesh Kujur
capsules.body: Sprinter Animesh Kujur set a new national 100 m record in 2025, becoming India's fastest man (as reported).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: World Para Athletics 2025
capsules.body: New Delhi hosted the 2025 World Para Athletics Championships in September-October 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Mohun Bagan ISL title
capsules.body: Mohun Bagan won the Indian Super League 2024-25 title (as reported).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Hockey Asia Cup 2025
capsules.body: India won the Men's Hockey Asia Cup 2025 at Rajgir, Bihar (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana
capsules.body: Announced in Budget 2025-26: converges schemes across 100 low-productivity districts to benefit 1.7 crore farmers, with focus on pulses and millets.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana
capsules.body: ₹99,446-crore scheme to generate 3.5 crore jobs through EPF-linked incentives for new hires, announced in 2025.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Gig workers welfare
capsules.body: Budget 2025-26: about 1 crore gig workers to be registered on e-Shram and given health cover under PM-JAY.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: One Nation One Subscription
capsules.body: Launched January 2025 with ₹6,000 crore for 2025-27: gives 6,300 government institutions access to 13,000 international e-journals via INFLIBNET.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: PM Internship Scheme
capsules.body: Offers 12-month internships in top 500 companies to youth aged 21-24, with ₹5,000 monthly stipend and ₹6,000 one-time grant; pilot launched October 2024.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Mission Mausam
capsules.body: Launched 14 January 2025 with ₹2,000-crore outlay to modernise weather forecasting, on IMD's 150th anniversary.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: G RAM G Bill 2025
capsules.body: The Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Bill, 2025 revamps MGNREGA, raising guaranteed rural employment from 100 to 125 days (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Income Tax Act 2025
capsules.body: Passed August 2025 and effective 1 April 2026, it replaces the 1961 Act, cutting sections from 819 to 536 with no change in tax rates.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Budget 2025 tax relief
capsules.body: Budget 2025-26 made income up to ₹12 lakh tax-free under the new regime; it was Nirmala Sitharaman's 8th consecutive budget.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: 8th Pay Commission
capsules.body: The government approved the 8th Central Pay Commission in January 2025.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Waqf Amendment Act 2025
capsules.body: Passed in April 2025, it amends the Waqf Act, 1995 to reform waqf property management.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025
capsules.body: Passed in 2025, it consolidates colonial-era immigration laws governing entry, stay and exit of foreigners (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Census 2027
capsules.body: Announced in 2025: India's next census will be the first fully digital census and will include caste enumeration.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: 16th Finance Commission
capsules.body: Chaired by Arvind Panagariya, the 16th Finance Commission's recommendations cover the 2026-31 period.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Atal Tinkering Labs
capsules.body: Budget 2025-26 announced 50,000 new Atal Tinkering Labs in schools to promote innovation.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: National Manufacturing Mission
capsules.body: Announced in Budget 2025-26 to boost domestic manufacturing across sectors (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Maritime Development Fund
capsules.body: Budget 2025-26 created a ₹25,000-crore Maritime Development Fund for the shipping sector (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Nuclear Energy Mission
capsules.body: Budget 2025-26 set a target of 100 GW nuclear capacity by 2047, promoting Small Modular Reactors (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Makhana Board
capsules.body: Budget 2025-26 announced a Makhana Board in Bihar to boost fox-nut production and processing.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Bharatiya Bhasha Pustak Scheme
capsules.body: Launched in 2025 to provide digital textbooks in Indian languages for schools and higher education (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: National Critical Mineral Mission
capsules.body: Approved in January 2025 to secure supply chains for minerals like lithium and cobalt (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Vibrant Villages Programme-II
capsules.body: Approved in 2025 with about ₹6,839-crore outlay for development of border villages (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Edible oils and pulses mission
capsules.body: The 2025 national mission targets self-sufficiency in edible oils and pulses through NAFED/NCCF procurement (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: National Sports Policy 2025
capsules.body: The Khelo Bharat Niti, approved in 2025, is India's new national sports policy (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Vocational skill labs
capsules.body: 1,200 vocational skill labs were launched in October 2025 across 400 Navodaya Vidyalayas and 200 Eklavya schools (as reported).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: GST 2.0
capsules.body: From 22 September 2025, GST moved largely to two slabs — 5% and 18% — with a 40% rate for sin and luxury goods (as reported).

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: CJI B. R. Gavai
capsules.body: Justice B. R. Gavai became the 52nd Chief Justice of India in May 2025 — the first Buddhist to hold the office (as reported).

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: CJI Surya Kant
capsules.body: Justice Surya Kant became the 53rd Chief Justice of India in November 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: CEC Gyanesh Kumar
capsules.body: Gyanesh Kumar became Chief Election Commissioner in February 2025, the first appointed under the 2023 selection law.

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: SEBI Chairperson
capsules.body: Tuhin Kanta Pandey became SEBI Chairperson in March 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: ISRO Chairman
capsules.body: V. Narayanan became ISRO Chairman in January 2025.

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: Delhi Chief Minister
capsules.body: Rekha Gupta became Delhi Chief Minister in February 2025 after the BJP won the assembly elections, returning to power in Delhi after 27 years.

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: Bihar elections 2025
capsules.body: The NDA won the November 2025 Bihar Assembly elections and Nitish Kumar returned as Chief Minister (as reported).

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: Pope Leo XIV
capsules.body: Cardinal Robert Prevost became Pope Leo XIV in May 2025 — the first American-born pope — after the death of Pope Francis on 21 April 2025.

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: US President
capsules.body: Donald Trump was inaugurated as the 47th US President on 20 January 2025.

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: Canada PM
capsules.body: Mark Carney became Prime Minister of Canada in March 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: Germany Chancellor
capsules.body: Friedrich Merz became Chancellor of Germany in May 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: South Korea President
capsules.body: Lee Jae-myung became President of South Korea in June 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: Australia PM
capsules.body: Anthony Albanese was re-elected Prime Minister of Australia in May 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: Japan PM
capsules.body: Sanae Takaichi became Japan's first woman Prime Minister in October 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: G20 Summit 2025
capsules.body: The 2025 G20 Summit was held at Johannesburg, South Africa — the first G20 summit on African soil (as reported).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: BRICS Summit 2025
capsules.body: The 2025 BRICS Summit was held at Rio de Janeiro; Indonesia joined BRICS as a full member in January 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: SCO Summit 2025
capsules.body: The 2025 SCO Summit was held at Tianjin, China, attended by PM Modi — his first China visit in seven years (as reported).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: AI Impact Summit 2026
capsules.body: India hosted the AI Impact Summit at New Delhi in February 2026, the fourth global AI summit after Bletchley, Seoul and Paris (as reported).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: COP30
capsules.body: The 2025 UN Climate Conference (COP30) was held at Belém, Brazil (as reported).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: Nepal protests 2025
capsules.body: Gen-Z protests in Nepal in September 2025 forced PM K. P. Sharma Oli to resign; Sushila Karki became interim PM (as reported).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: Kailash Yatra resumes
capsules.body: The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra resumed in 2025 after a five-year gap (as reported).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: WAVES 2025
capsules.body: India hosted the first World Audio Visual and Entertainment Summit (WAVES) at Mumbai in May 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas 2025
capsules.body: The 18th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas was held at Bhubaneswar, Odisha, in January 2025.

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: G7 Summit 2025
capsules.body: The 2025 G7 Summit was held at Kananaskis, Canada, with PM Modi attending as an outreach guest (as reported).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: Dalai Lama at 90
capsules.body: The Dalai Lama turned 90 in July 2025 and issued a statement on his succession (as reported).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: US tariffs on India
capsules.body: In 2025 the US imposed 50% tariffs on Indian goods — 25% reciprocal plus 25% over Russian oil purchases (as reported).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: SpaDeX docking
capsules.body: On 16 January 2025 ISRO's SpaDeX mission docked two satellites in orbit, making India the fourth country with space-docking capability after the US, Russia and China.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: SpaDeX undocking
capsules.body: ISRO completed the SpaDeX undocking manoeuvre in March 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: NISAR launch
capsules.body: The NASA-ISRO NISAR earth-observation satellite was launched by GSLV-F16 from Sriharikota on 30 July 2025 — the first satellite with dual-frequency (L- and S-band) radar.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: ISRO 100th launch
capsules.body: ISRO's 100th launch was the GSLV-F15/NVS-02 mission on 29 January 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: EOS-09
capsules.body: ISRO's EOS-09 earth-observation satellite launch on PSLV-C61 failed in May 2025 due to a third-stage anomaly (as reported).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: CMS-03
capsules.body: ISRO launched the CMS-03 (GSAT-7R) communication satellite in November 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Sarvam AI model
capsules.body: Under the IndiaAI Mission, Sarvam was selected in 2025 to build India's first sovereign large language model (as reported).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Shubhanshu Shukla
capsules.body: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the International Space Station on the Axiom-4 mission in June 2025 — the first Indian to reach the ISS (as reported).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Sunita Williams return
capsules.body: Astronaut Sunita Williams returned to Earth in March 2025 aboard SpaceX Crew-9 after an extended ISS stay (as reported).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Genome India
capsules.body: The Genome India Project completed sequencing of 10,000 Indian genomes in 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Bharatiya Antariksh Station
capsules.body: India targets setting up the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and a crewed moon landing by 2040.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: National Space Day
capsules.body: India observes National Space Day on 23 August, marking the Chandrayaan-3 landing; the second edition was celebrated in 2025.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India 4th largest economy
capsules.body: India overtook Japan in 2025 to become the world's fourth-largest economy in nominal GDP terms (as reported).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: GDP growth FY25
capsules.body: India's GDP grew 6.5% in FY 2024-25, the fastest among major economies (as reported).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI rate cuts
capsules.body: The RBI cut the repo rate by 100 basis points between February and June 2025, from 6.5% to 5.5% (as reported).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: UPI
capsules.body: UPI remained the world's largest instant-payment system by transaction volume in 2025.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India-EFTA TEPA
capsules.body: The India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement came into force on 1 October 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Forex reserves
capsules.body: India's foreign exchange reserves hovered around $700 billion through 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Startup ecosystem
capsules.body: India remained the world's third-largest startup ecosystem in 2025.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India-UK FTA
capsules.body: The India-UK Free Trade Agreement was signed in July 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Budget 2026-27
capsules.body: Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Union Budget 2026-27 on 1 February 2026 — her ninth consecutive budget (as reported).

capsules.subject: Books
capsules.title: Arundhati Roy memoir
capsules.body: Booker winner Arundhati Roy published her memoir 'Mother Mary Comes to Me' in 2025.

capsules.subject: Books
capsules.title: Kiran Desai novel
capsules.body: Kiran Desai's novel 'The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny' was shortlisted for the 2025 Booker Prize (as reported).

capsules.subject: Books
capsules.title: Krasznahorkai works
capsules.body: 2025 Nobel laureate László Krasznahorkai is known for novels like 'Satantango' and 'The Melancholy of Resistance'.

capsules.subject: Books
capsules.title: Heart Lamp
capsules.body: Banu Mushtaq's 'Heart Lamp', translated from Kannada by Deepa Bhasthi, won the 2025 International Booker Prize.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Operation Sindoor
capsules.body: On the night of 6-7 May 2025, India struck nine terror targets in Pakistan and PoK in Operation Sindoor, in response to the 22 April Pahalgam attack in which 26 tourists were killed.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Sindoor ceasefire
capsules.body: After a four-day military confrontation, India and Pakistan agreed to a ceasefire on 10 May 2025, ending Operation Sindoor hostilities.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: S-400 record kill
capsules.body: During Operation Sindoor, an IAF S-400 unit destroyed a Pakistani aircraft from 314 km — described as the longest surface-to-air kill (as reported).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Indus Waters Treaty
capsules.body: India held the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance in April 2025 following the Pahalgam terror attack.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Operation Brahma
capsules.body: India launched Operation Brahma in March 2025 to deliver relief after the devastating Myanmar earthquake (as reported).

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Republic Day 2025
capsules.body: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto was the chief guest at India's 76th Republic Day in 2025.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Maha Kumbh 2025
capsules.body: The Maha Kumbh was held at Prayagraj in January-February 2025.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Maratha Military Landscapes
capsules.body: UNESCO inscribed India's Maratha Military Landscapes as a World Heritage Site in 2025 — India's 44th (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Cheetahs from Botswana
capsules.body: Eight cheetahs arrived from Botswana in February 2025 under Project Cheetah (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: IMD 150 years
capsules.body: The India Meteorological Department completed 150 years in January 2025.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Vande Mataram 150
capsules.body: November 2025 marked 150 years of 'Vande Mataram', written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in 1875 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: RSS 100 years
capsules.body: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh completed 100 years in 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: UN Year of Cooperatives
capsules.body: The United Nations declared 2025 the International Year of Cooperatives.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: UN Year of Quantum
capsules.body: 2025 was also the UN International Year of Quantum Science and Technology, marking 100 years of quantum mechanics.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Digital India 10 years
capsules.body: July 2025 marked 10 years of the Digital India programme (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Skill India 10 years
capsules.body: The Skill India Mission completed 10 years in July 2025; it includes PMKVY training and the Skill India Digital Hub (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Chenab Rail Bridge
capsules.body: The Chenab Rail Bridge — the world's highest railway arch bridge — was inaugurated in June 2025, completing the Kashmir rail link (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Z-Morh Tunnel
capsules.body: The Z-Morh Tunnel at Sonamarg, ensuring all-weather connectivity to Ladakh, was inaugurated in January 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Pamban Bridge
capsules.body: India's first vertical-lift sea bridge, the new Pamban Bridge in Tamil Nadu, was inaugurated in April 2025 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Vande Bharat to Srinagar
capsules.body: Vande Bharat trains began running to Srinagar in June 2025 over the USBRL Kashmir rail link (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Electoral roll revision
capsules.body: The Election Commission carried out a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Bihar in 2025 ahead of the assembly polls (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Yoga Day 2025
capsules.body: The 11th International Day of Yoga (21 June 2025) was led from Visakhapatnam (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Beti Bachao 10 years
capsules.body: January 2025 marked 10 years of the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: PM Mudra 10 years
capsules.body: April 2025 marked 10 years of the PM Mudra Yojana for micro-enterprise loans (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: NEP 2020 five years
capsules.body: July 2025 marked five years of the National Education Policy 2020 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Gyan Bharatam Mission
capsules.body: The Gyan Bharatam Mission for survey, documentation and conservation of India's manuscripts was announced in Budget 2025-26 (as reported).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games 2026: women's cricket gold
capsules.body: On 22 September 2026, India's women's cricket team won India's first gold at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, thrashing Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final at Nisshin — the biggest winning margin in women's T20I history.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Record 217 in Asian Games final
capsules.body: India posted 216/3 against Sri Lanka in the 2026 Asian Games women's final — setting Sri Lanka a 217-run target — the highest total in Asian Games women's cricket history; Smriti Mandhana made 79 off 45 and Richa Ghosh an unbeaten 49 off 22, and Sri Lanka were bowled out for 69.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Mandhana crosses 11,000 international runs
capsules.body: Smriti Mandhana completed 11,000 runs in international cricket during India's Asian Games 2026 final win over Sri Lanka on 22 September 2026.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Sri Lanka 69 all out in final
capsules.body: Chasing 217 in the Asian Games 2026 women's final, Sri Lanka collapsed to 69 all out in 15.4 overs; Deepti Sharma took 3/6 and Pakistan took bronze by beating Bangladesh by 31 runs.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Kohli reaches 15,000 ODI runs
capsules.body: On 27 September 2026, Virat Kohli became only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar to reach 15,000 ODI runs, hitting an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls as India beat West Indies in the first ODI — his 86th international century.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Gill's 10th ODI hundred
capsules.body: Shubman Gill struck 110 off 108 balls — his 10th ODI century — in India's eight-wicket win over West Indies in the first ODI on 27 September 2026, chasing 296 with 50 balls to spare.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Badminton men's team confirms medal
capsules.body: India's men's badminton team beat Japan 3-0 in the Asian Games 2026 quarter-final on 22 September 2026, confirming a medal in consecutive editions for the first time since 1986.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Roshibina Devi's third straight podium
capsules.body: Wushu star Roshibina Devi reached the women's 60kg semi-final at the Asian Games 2026, securing her third consecutive Asian Games podium.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Hockey: India 16-1 Sri Lanka
capsules.body: India's men's hockey team beat Sri Lanka 16-1 in their Pool A match at the Asian Games 2026.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Kabaddi: India beats South Korea 63-31
capsules.body: India's men's kabaddi team defeated South Korea 63-31 in their Group A match at the Asian Games 2026.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: ISRO launches EOS-05 on GSLV-F17
capsules.body: On 4 September 2026, ISRO launched the 2,367-kg Earth observation satellite EOS-05 aboard GSLV-F17 from Sriharikota — India's first imaging satellite designed to operate from geosynchronous orbit, about 36,000 km up; it was the 19th GSLV flight.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: ISRO-ESA cooperation extended to 2032
capsules.body: ISRO and the European Space Agency renewed their space cooperation until 2032 at the International Space Summit in Paris on 9-10 September 2026, covering missions including Aditya-L1, Proba-3 and the upcoming Chandrayaan-5.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: DRDO pact for quantum dilution refrigerator
capsules.body: DRDO signed a pact with Zero mK India to indigenously develop a 20 millikelvin dilution refrigerator for quantum computing (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: IIEST Shibpur-TCS AI Centre of Excellence
capsules.body: IIEST Shibpur and TCS launched a state-of-the-art Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Project DRISHTI: AI for freight wagons
capsules.body: Northeast Frontier Railway and IIT Guwahati introduced 'Project DRISHTI', an AI-based system to monitor freight wagon doors, locks and seals (September 2026).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: ADB raises India FY27 growth forecast to 7%
capsules.body: In its September 2026 Asian Development Outlook update, the ADB raised India's real GDP growth forecast for FY27 to 7.0% from 6.6% — a 40-basis-point upgrade.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI holds repo rate at 5.25%
capsules.body: The RBI kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% in its August 2026 policy — the fourth straight pause — retaining a neutral stance; Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the next MPC meet is scheduled for 5-7 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: S&P and Fitch raise India growth forecasts
capsules.body: S&P raised India's FY27 GDP forecast to 7% (from 6.6%) and Fitch to 6.9% (from 6.4%) in September 2026; Fitch expects the repo rate to rise to 5.5% in October.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: 55 Indian cities in fastest-growing top 100
capsules.body: The Oxford Economics 2026 Global Cities Index placed 55 Indian cities among the world's top 100 fastest-growing city economies (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI directions on REIT/InvIT valuation
capsules.body: The RBI issued directions altering valuation norms for REITs and InvITs (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: SBI Card's FD-backed credit cards
capsules.body: SBI Card launched 'Advantage SBI Card', fixed-deposit-backed secured credit cards, on the YONO app (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Samvriddhi gets PA-Online nod
capsules.body: Samvriddhi Inclusive received the RBI's in-principle approval to operate as a payment aggregator (online) (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: PayGlocal's GIFT City approval
capsules.body: PayGlocal secured in-principle approval from IFSCA to set up a payment service provider in GIFT City (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Screen protectors under BIS compulsory registration
capsules.body: MeitY brought smartphone screen protectors and tempered glass under the BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme via gazette notification in September 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Delhi airport 28th in global connectivity
capsules.body: Delhi airport ranked 28th in the OAG Megahubs 2026 global connectivity ranking (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: IEA: India's electrification to hit 32% by 2035
capsules.body: An IEA report (September 2026) projects India's electrification rate could rise from 19% to 32% by 2035.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: DDU-GKY 2.0: 70,000 rural youth to be trained
capsules.body: About 70,000 rural youth across 24 states and UTs are expected to begin placement-linked skill training under DDU-GKY 2.0 from October 2026 (Ministry of Rural Development announcement, 25 September 2026), aligned with the National Skill Qualification Framework.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: PFRDA guidelines for NPS Swasthya
capsules.body: PFRDA issued operational guidelines for NPS Swasthya, its health insurance scheme (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: UP launches Bharat Taxi
capsules.body: Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath launched 'Bharat Taxi' in September 2026.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana
capsules.body: Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath launched the 'Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana' for farmers in September 2026.

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Rs 320 crore Kurukshetra ITI cluster under PM-SETU
capsules.body: The National Steering Committee approved the Kurukshetra ITI cluster for Rs 320 crore under PM-SETU (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: AFSPA extended in Northeast for six months
capsules.body: The Centre extended AFSPA in specified areas of Manipur, Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh for another six months from 1 October 2026 after a law-and-order review.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: ECI's roll revision: 13 crore+ names struck off
capsules.body: The Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls — begun in Bihar in June 2025 — has struck over 13 crore names from draft rolls across 30 states and UTs (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: UFBU–IBA talks defer three-day bank strike
capsules.body: The United Forum of Bank Unions deferred its planned three-day nationwide bank strike (28–30 September 2026) after a 27 September meeting with the Indian Banks' Association agreed to form a joint IBA–UFBU committee on the five-day banking demand; September salaries had been disbursed early on 25 September.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: New Amrit Bharat Express: Bhuj-Barauni
capsules.body: Indian Railways approved a tri-weekly Amrit Bharat Express between Bhuj (Gujarat) and Barauni (Bihar), covering 2,532 km across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar (September 2026).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: SC orders sealing of 16,000+ Meerut properties
capsules.body: The Supreme Court ordered the sealing of over 16,000 properties and demolition of illegal structures in Meerut (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: 150 years of Vande Mataram in 2026
capsules.body: The Centre is organising year-long programmes in 2026 to mark 150 years of the national song Vande Mataram.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: ICG ship Shaunak sails for Australia
capsules.body: Indian Coast Guard ship Shaunak sailed for Australia with QUAD officers on board (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: ICAI's SSA 5000 sustainability standard
capsules.body: The ICAI issued 'SSA 5000' to align sustainability assurance with global standards (reported September 2026).

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: UNGA 81: Lavrov backs India for permanent UNSC seat
capsules.body: At the 81st UN General Assembly in September 2026, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov backed India and Brazil's bids for permanent UN Security Council seats.

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: Jaishankar's terrorism warning at UNGA
capsules.body: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar told the 81st UNGA in September 2026 that attempts to normalise terrorism and avoid its consequences would not be accepted, calling Pakistan a 'serial practitioner of terrorism'.

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: Trump hosts Xi at White House state dinner
capsules.body: US President Donald Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping at a White House state dinner on 24 September 2026.

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: Pope Leo XIV's first visit to France
capsules.body: Pope Leo XIV — the first American pope, elected in the 2025 conclave — began a four-day apostolic visit to France on 25 September 2026, warning on AI and nuclear arms and defending press freedom.

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: EU-Philippines reach FTA breakthrough
capsules.body: The EU and the Philippines reached a 'substantial agreement' on a comprehensive free trade agreement in September 2026, ending a decade of stop-start talks that began in 2015.

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: US-China agree AI communication channel
capsules.body: The US and China agreed in September 2026 to set up a communication channel for handling incidents involving artificial intelligence.

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: Denmark-US deal defuses Greenland crisis
capsules.body: Denmark and the US signed a deal on Greenland in September 2026, de-escalating a months-long diplomatic crisis over the Arctic territory.

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: Abbas addresses 81st UNGA
capsules.body: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas delivered a pre-recorded address to the 81st UN General Assembly on 24 September 2026.

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: Bangkok hit by floods
capsules.body: Residents of Bangkok waded through flooded streets after heavy rain on 26 September 2026.

capsules.subject: World
capsules.title: Germany ready for submarine deal with India
capsules.body: Germany's Ambassador to India said in September 2026 that Berlin is ready to sign a 'forward-leaning' submarine deal with India.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Tarang Shakti-26 at Jodhpur
capsules.body: The IAF's multinational air exercise Tarang Shakti-26 runs at Air Force Station Jodhpur from 26 September to 12 October 2026, with around 40 countries participating.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-I from 30 September 2026
capsules.body: The SSC's CGL 2026 Tier-I computer-based exam runs 30 September to 30 October 2026 for 12,256 Group B & C posts; the exam city intimation slip went live on 22 September 2026 and admit cards download 2–3 days before each candidate's exam date.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: SSC CGL 2026 detailed vacancy notice out
capsules.body: The Staff Selection Commission released the detailed post-wise vacancy notice for CGL 2026 on 24 September 2026, announcing 12,256 vacancies for Group B and Group C posts across ministries and departments.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India's first shooting gold at Asian Games 2026
capsules.body: Suruchi Inder Singh and Kamaljeet won gold in the 10m air pistol mixed team event on 25 September 2026 at Aichi-Nagoya, setting an Asian record — India's first shooting gold of the Games.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Gulveer's 10,000m silver; Baranica's historic bronze
capsules.body: On 25 September 2026, Gulveer Singh won silver in the men's 10,000m — the first Indian to win multiple 10,000m medals at the Asian Games — while Baranica Elangovan's bronze was the first-ever pole vault podium for an Indian at a major multi-sport event.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Kabaddi double gold on 26 September 2026
capsules.body: Both the Indian men's and women's kabaddi teams defended their Asian Games titles on 26 September 2026, beating Iran in both finals; India won 7 medals that day to reach 30 overall (4 gold, 12 silver, 14 bronze).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: TN's Thaimaaman gold ring scheme launches 28 September
capsules.body: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches the 'Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam' on 28 September 2026 in Madurai: every newborn delivered in a government hospital gets a one-gram, 22-carat gold ring; the first phase covers 1.28 lakh rings with an annual outlay of ₹755.83 crore.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: BCCI signs ₹150 crore title sponsor deal
capsules.body: On 25 September 2026 the BCCI signed a ₹150 crore title sponsorship deal with Muthoot FinCorp for international home matches, running till March 2028.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Two new offshore mineral blocks near Great Nicobar
capsules.body: In September 2026 the government notified two more offshore mineral blocks — West Sewell Ridge-01 and Sewell Rise-01 — for licensing near Great Nicobar Island in the Andaman Sea, an area rich in polymetallic nodules.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: SSC CGL Tier-I admit cards out from 27 September
capsules.body: The Staff Selection Commission began releasing SSC CGL 2026 Tier-I admit cards on 27 September 2026 in phases — each candidate’s admission certificate goes live 2–3 days before their exam date. The CBT runs 30 September–30 October 2026 for 12,256 tentative Group B and Group C posts; city intimation slips were issued on 21 September.

capsules.subject: Appointments
capsules.title: Mandeep K. Bhandari is new CBSE Chairperson
capsules.body: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved Mandeep K. Bhandari, a 2001-batch AGMUT-cadre IAS officer, as Chairperson of the CBSE. Earlier Principal Secretary to the J&K Lieutenant Governor, he replaces Lokhande Prashant Sitaram, who held additional charge after Rahul Singh’s transfer in June 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: OECD raises India’s FY27 growth forecast to 7.1%
capsules.body: In its September 2026 Interim Economic Outlook ‘Weathering Successive Shocks’, the OECD raised India’s FY27 GDP growth forecast by 80 basis points to 7.1% (from 6.3% in June), citing resilient domestic demand; FY28 growth is seen moderating to 6.5%.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Asian Games 2026: India reaches 39 medals on 28 September
capsules.body: India’s tally at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 reached 39 medals (4 gold, 17 silver, 18 bronze) on 28 September 2026, after Esha Singh’s silver in the women’s 25m pistol and Pincky Balhara’s kurash bronze; seven medals had come on 27 September. Central cash awards: Rs 30 lakh (gold), Rs 20 lakh (silver), Rs 10 lakh (bronze).

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: WorldSkills Shanghai 2026: India finishes 10th, best ever
capsules.body: India placed 10th at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 — its best performance ever — winning six silver medals and 20 Medals for Excellence, improving on 13th place at Lyon 2024 (four bronze).

capsules.subject: Schemes
capsules.title: Livestock Insurance Portal launched on 28 September
capsules.body: Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) launched the Livestock Insurance Portal of the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying in New Delhi on 28 September 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India-New Zealand FTA in force from 20 October 2026
capsules.body: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement comes into force on 20 October 2026, giving 100% duty-free access to Indian exports.

capsules.subject: SSC Exams
capsules.title: SSC CGL Tier-1 admit cards rolling out region-wise; exam from 30 Sep
capsules.body: SSC CGL 2026 Tier-1 begins 30 September 2026 and runs till 30 October in three daily shifts; region-wise admit cards are being released on the regional SSC websites. The paper has 100 questions for 200 marks across four 25-question sections, a 1-hour duration, 15-minute sectional timers and 0.50 negative marking; about 12,256 vacancies are on offer.

capsules.subject: SSC Exams
capsules.title: SSC CHSL 2026: 2,536 posts; apply by 7 October
capsules.body: SSC has invited applications for the Combined Higher Secondary Level (CHSL) 2026 examination for 2,536 LDC/JSA and DEO posts. Applications close 7 October 2026; the correction window runs 14–16 October 2026 on ssc.gov.in.

capsules.subject: SSC Exams
capsules.title: SSC CGL Tier-1 pattern refresher: 100 questions, 200 marks, −0.50
capsules.body: SSC CGL Tier-1 (from 30 September 2026) carries 100 objective questions for 200 marks across four sections — General Intelligence & Reasoning, General Awareness, Quantitative Aptitude and English Comprehension — with a 60-minute limit and negative marking of 0.50 per wrong answer.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Bank strike of 28–30 September deferred after IBA–UFBU talks
capsules.body: The United Forum of Bank Unions deferred its 28–30 September 2026 strike after talks with the IBA: banks agreed to five-day banking twice a month for non-field staff, with a further meeting in October. The strike would have affected about 8.5 lakh employees.

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: NTA: lost or damaged scorecards can be re-issued
capsules.body: NTA's 23 September 2026 notice says candidates whose NEET-UG, JEE-Main, CUET or other NTA scorecards are lost, stolen or damaged should first check DigiLocker for a digitally verified copy; if unavailable, they can apply in the prescribed Annexure-I format with identity documents via result@nta.gov.in.

capsules.subject: Vacancies
capsules.title: SSC CHSL 2026: 2,536 posts; apply by 7 October
capsules.body: SSC notified 2,536 tentative CHSL (10+2) posts; apply online 7 September-7 October 2026 on ssc.gov.in. Age 18-27 as on 1 August 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: August IIP grows 8.0%; manufacturing 9.0%
