capsules.body: India's IIP grew 8.0% year-on-year in August 2026, with manufacturing output up 9.0%.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: World Heart Day: 'Don't Miss a Beat'
capsules.body: World Heart Day was observed on 29 September 2026 with the campaign theme 'Don't Miss a Beat'.

capsules.subject: IR
capsules.title: India-China ties: the 'three mutuals'
capsules.body: The MEA said India-China ties advance under mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity, per leaders' guidance at the BRICS summit.

capsules.subject: Sci-Tech
capsules.title: EOS-05: first Indian imaging satellite for GEO
capsules.body: ISRO's EOS-05 (2,367 kg), launched 4 Sep 2026 on GSLV-F17 into Sub-GTO, is India's first imaging satellite designed for geosynchronous orbit.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Vithya Ramraj breaks P.T. Usha's 1984 record
capsules.body: Vithya Ramraj won 400m hurdles bronze in 54.75s, breaking P.T. Usha's 55.42s national record from 1984.

capsules.subject: Misc
capsules.title: Steel Industry Safety Council announced
capsules.body: The Ministry of Steel on 30 September 2026 announced the Steel Industry Safety Council (SISC), an apex safety body chaired by Secretary Sandeep Poundrik, with a Steel Industry Safety Directorate for audits and incident investigation.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: India's first Blue Bond: Rs 600 crore
capsules.body: Sagarmala Finance Corporation launched India's first Blue Bond on 28 September 2026: Rs 600 crore with a Rs 500 crore green-shoe option, 10-year tenor, AA+ rated by ICRA and CARE, arranged by SBI Capital Markets.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Net FDI hits five-year high: USD 13.4 billion
capsules.body: India's net FDI hit a five-year high of USD 13.4 billion in April-July 2026, up 38% year-on-year; gross inflows rose 12.6% to USD 43.9 billion.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: ECI relaxes Form 6 rule in non-SIR states
capsules.body: The Election Commission on 30 September 2026 reverted to allowing online Form 6 submission — used for fresh voter registration — without the attached declaration in states where the special intensive revision of electoral rolls is not underway.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: ISRO targets seven launches by March 2027
capsules.body: ISRO Chairman V Narayanan said on 30 September the agency targets seven rocket launches by March 2027, including Gaganyaan's first uncrewed flight, using PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 rockets.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Bodhana Sivanandan, 11, youngest Woman Grandmaster
capsules.body: Eleven-year-old Bodhana Sivanandan became the youngest Woman Grandmaster in chess history, as reported on 30 September 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Cabinet approves Rs 1.86 lakh crore PM-DHARA
capsules.body: The Union Cabinet on 1 October 2026 approved the PM-DHARA scheme to build intra-state power transmission networks with battery storage, aimed at transferring 135 GW of clean renewable energy.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Wheat MSP raised to Rs 2,610/quintal for 2027-28
capsules.body: The Centre raised the wheat MSP by Rs 25 to Rs 2,610 per quintal for the 2027-28 marketing year; pulses and oilseeds received hikes of up to Rs 675 per quintal.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: India's archery clean sweep at Asian Games 2026
capsules.body: India won all three compound archery team golds at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya on 30 September: the women's team beat China 238-234, equalling the world record set by Korea at Incheon 2014; the mixed team beat South Korea 158-157 in a shoot-off; the men's team also won gold. India stands eighth with 60 medals.

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: IISc Bengaluru tops Indian institutions in THE World University Rankings 2027
capsules.body: IISc Bengaluru emerged as the highest-ranked Indian institution in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2027, reported on 1 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Education
capsules.title: New NCERT Class 9 textbook links institution mottos to ancient heritage
capsules.body: A new NCERT Class 9 social science textbook highlights how mottos of modern Indian institutions, including Satyamev Jayate, originate from the Upanishads and the Mahabharata.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: Navy to commission 18 warships in 2026
capsules.body: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told the Navy's Commanders Conference in New Delhi that the Indian Navy will commission 18 warships in 2026, calling it 'a year for the Indian Navy'.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: Reform Utsav launched 2 October
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — PM Modi inaugurated 'Reform Utsav' on 2 October 2026 — a first-of-its-kind campaign celebrating reforms across ministries, marking 12 years of transformative governance; the MHA's counter-terrorism policy 'PRAHAAR' (February 2026) is featured.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: Special Campaign 6.0: 2–31 October
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — Special Campaign 6.0 runs 2–31 October 2026 with focus on Swachhata, reducing pendency and scientific e-waste disposal in government offices; phases: preparatory 15–30 Sept, implementation 2–31 Oct, evaluation 16–30 Nov.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI MPC 5–7 Oct: hike likely
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — 35 of 61 economists in a Reuters poll expect the RBI to raise the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% at the 5–7 October MPC meeting — the first hike since February 2023; repo currently 5.25%; August CPI 4.82%.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Chess Olympiad: India Open silver
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — At the 46th Chess Olympiad (Samarkand), India took Open silver (gold: Uzbekistan) and women's bronze (gold: China), defending the Nona Gaprindashvili Trophy for the third straight edition; Savitha Shri B won individual gold on board 5.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Special gram sabhas on 2 October
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — Special gram sabhas were held nationwide on 2 October 2026, launching the People's Plan Campaign 2026-27 ('Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas') under which gram panchayats prepare GPDPs for 2027-28.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: ISRO: Gaganyaan G1 this year
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — ISRO Chairman V Narayanan (4 September 2026) said the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission (G1) is targeted for this calendar year after about 8,000 tests; three uncrewed missions precede the 2027 crewed mission; Kulasekarapattinam pad ready by March 2027.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Nobel Medicine 2026: optogenetics
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries on light-gated ion channels and optogenetics (prize: 12 million Swedish kronor).

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Nobel Physics 2026: IceCube
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Nobel Chemistry 2026: asymmetric synthesis
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI: repo at 5.50%
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — RBI's MPC raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% at its 5–7 Oct meeting; stance 'Calibrated Tightening'; FY27 GDP 7.1%, CPI 5.2%.

capsules.subject: Sports
capsules.title: Smriti Mandhana: white-ball captain
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — BCCI named Smriti Mandhana the full-time white-ball captain of the India women's team after Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down across formats on 6 Oct 2026.

capsules.subject: Defence
capsules.title: IAF Day: 8 October
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — The Indian Air Force, established in 1932, celebrates its raising day on 8 October; Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit takes over as Chief on 31 Oct 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: SME Growth Fund: Rs 10,000 crore
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The Union Cabinet (6 October 2026) approved a Rs 10,000-crore commitment to an Alternative Investment Fund under the SME Growth Fund framework, giving growth-stage SMEs long-term equity capital; announced in Budget 2026-27, prioritising manufacturing and Tier-II/III clusters.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: ITLA approved as apex transport body
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The Cabinet approved the Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) as an SPV — the apex body for integrated transport planning, research, project appraisal and monitoring.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: GST Council: decriminalisation push
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The 57th GST Council (8 October) recommended removing GST officers' arrest powers, raising the prosecution threshold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore, scrapping minimum punishments and cutting the general penalty from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Uttarakhand: sixth fully literate state
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — Uttarakhand was declared India's sixth fully literate state (after Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh and Sikkim) under NEP 2020 and the ULLAS–Nav Bharat Saaksharta Programme on 6 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Health
capsules.title: JOSH teams launched for TB elimination
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — J.P. Nadda launched JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) teams at Bharat Mandapam on 8 October 2026: five NCC cadets plus five MY Bharat volunteers per team under a Class-I officer, first in 55 districts across 11 states.

capsules.subject: Science
capsules.title: Nobel Chemistry 2026: Kagan and Soai
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to Henri B. Kagan (France) and Kenso Soai (Japan) for pioneering discoveries of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

capsules.subject: General Awareness
capsules.title: SSC GD Constable 2026 result out: 1,97,033 shortlisted for PET/PST (12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Staff Selection Commission declared the SSC GD Constable 2026 result on 12 October 2026. Of 21,56,776 candidates who appeared in the CBT (27 April–30 May 2026), 1,97,033 were shortlisted for the next stage — the Physical Efficiency Test / Physical Standard Test (PET/PST). Shortlisted candidates include 15,782 female and 1,81,251 male candidates, plus 375 additional male candidates for SSF. Cut-off marks were released with the result write-up. Check roll numbers in the PDF merit lists on ssc.gov.in.

capsules.subject: General Awareness
capsules.title: SSC CHSL 2025 final result declared: 3,515 recommended (7 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The SSC declared the final result of the Combined Higher Secondary (10+2) Level Examination, 2025 on 7 October 2026, provisionally recommending 3,515 candidates against 3,522 reported vacancies for Lower Division Clerk (LDC), Junior Secretariat Assistant (JSA) and Data Entry Operator (DEO) posts. The result followed the first round of tentative allocation (17 August 2026) and the sliding/identity verification process (1–3 September 2026). Final allocation was on a merit-cum-preference basis; detailed marks and the final answer key will be uploaded on ssc.gov.in separately.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: RBI MPC October 2026: repo 5.50%, calibrated tightening, GDP 7.1%
capsules.body: The RBI’s MPC on 7 October 2026 hiked the policy repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% — the first increase since February 2023 — and moved the stance from neutral to ‘calibrated tightening’ (4–2). Consequential rates: SDF 5.25%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%. Governor Sanjay Malhotra cited West Asia conflict-driven crude volatility and food/fuel/fertiliser pressures. Projections for FY27: real GDP growth 7.1% (up from 6.7%), CPI inflation 5.2%; August CPI stood at 4.82%.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Odisha Cabinet: free textbooks for 28.7 lakh students (13 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Odisha Cabinet on 13 October 2026 approved free textbooks for about 28.7 lakh students of Classes 9 and 10 in government and aided secondary schools (SC/ST students were already covered). The scheme runs five years, 2025-26 to 2029-30, with an outlay of Rs 284.07 crore. The Cabinet also cleared a Rs 500-crore urban drainage programme to tackle flooding.

capsules.subject: Environment
capsules.title: International Big Cat Alliance HQ inaugurated in New Delhi (12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav inaugurated the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) headquarters at 55 Lodhi Estate, New Delhi, on 12 October 2026. IBCA is a treaty-based intergovernmental organisation for the seven big cats — tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma. The Union Cabinet approved it on 29 February 2024 with Rs 150 crore over five years (2023-24 to 2027-28); 29 countries, including India, are members.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Cabinet approves 78 days’ productivity-linked bonus for 11.40 lakh railway staff
capsules.body: In October 2026 the Union Cabinet approved 78 days’ productivity-linked bonus for 11.40 lakh railway employees, up to ₹17,951 per employee, following the Railways’ strong performance in 2025–26.

capsules.subject: Polity
capsules.title: Prakash Rajpurohit appointed Deputy Election Commissioner till 8 April 2030
capsules.body: Prakash Rajpurohit, a 2010-batch Rajasthan-cadre IAS officer, was appointed Deputy Election Commissioner with tenure until 8 April 2030, as the Centre approved 27 appointments at joint secretary and equivalent levels in October 2026.

capsules.subject: Economy
capsules.title: Ramesh Chand-led panel to review sugar MSP and farmers’ returns
capsules.body: The Centre has set up a committee headed by Ramesh Chand to review the minimum selling price of sugar and farmers’ returns, examining sugar production costs, mill viability, cane weighing practices and deductions for mechanically harvested sugarcane.

capsules.subject: Governance
capsules.title: PM GatiShakti National Master Plan completes five years
capsules.body: The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan completed five years on 13 October 2026 (launched 13 October 2021), marking progress in integrated infrastructure planning across ministries and states.

oneliners.text: The Great Bath was discovered at Mohenjo-daro, excavated in the 1920s; the bronze 'Dancing Girl' also comes from Mohenjo-daro.
Harappa was the first Indus site excavated (1921) by Daya Ram Sahni; Mohenjo-daro was excavated by R. D. Banerji in 1922.
Lothal in Gujarat had the world's earliest known dockyard, proving Harappan maritime trade.
Dholavira (Gujarat) is the only Indus city divided into three parts and is famous for advanced water management; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2021).
Surkotada (Gujarat) yielded the first actual remains of horse bones from a Harappan context.
Kalibangan (Rajasthan) is known for the world's earliest ploughed field and a distinctive bangle factory.
Chanhudaro (Sindh) was a centre of bead-making and shell-working and had no citadel.
Rakhigarhi in Haryana is the largest Harappan site excavated in India.
Banawali (Haryana) shows town planning without radial streets and yielded a toy plough.
Alamgirpur (Uttar Pradesh) is the easternmost known Harappan site.
Sutkagendor (Makran coast, Pakistan) is the westernmost Harappan site.
Daimabad (Maharashtra) is the southernmost Harappan site, famous for bronze sculptures.
The Rig Veda has 10 mandalas and 1028 suktas; the Gayatri Mantra appears in its 3rd mandala, addressed to Savitri.
The Purusha Sukta, describing the four varnas, is found in the 10th mandala of the Rig Veda.
The Sama Veda is the veda of chants and melodies and is the origin of Indian music.
The Yajur Veda deals with sacrificial rituals and procedures.
The Atharva Veda contains charms, spells and early medical knowledge; the Sabha and Samiti are mentioned in it.
There are 108 Upanishads; 'Satyameva Jayate' is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad.
The Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna) was fought on the banks of the Parushni (Ravi) between King Sudas of the Bharatas and a confederacy of ten tribes.
In later Vedic times Janaka ruled Videha with his capital at Mithila; Yajnavalkya and Gargi were scholars of his court.
Of the 16 Mahajanapadas, Magadha emerged the most powerful, with its early capital at Rajagriha.
Bimbisara of the Haryanka dynasty was the first historical king of Magadha and a contemporary of the Buddha.
Ajatashatru killed his father Bimbisara, convened the First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha and fortified Pataliputra.
Udayin, son of Ajatashatru, founded the city of Pataliputra at the confluence of the Ganga and Son.
Mahapadma Nanda, the first Nanda king, was called 'destroyer of Kshatriyas' and the first non-Kshatriya king of Magadha.
Alexander invaded India in 326 BCE and defeated Porus (Puru) at the Battle of Hydaspes on the Jhelum.
Alexander died in 323 BCE at Babylon; his Indian campaign ended at the Beas where his troops mutinied.
Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire in 321 BCE after overthrowing Dhanananda, guided by Chanakya (Kautilya).
Kautilya's Arthashastra is the classic Mauryan treatise on statecraft, economics and espionage.
Seleucus Nicator was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya (c. 303 BCE); his ambassador Megasthenes wrote 'Indica'.
Ashoka's remorse after the Kalinga War (261 BCE) is recorded in his 13th Major Rock Edict.
James Prinsep deciphered Ashoka's Brahmi inscriptions in 1837.
The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath was adopted as India's National Emblem on 26 January 1950.
Ashoka appointed Dhamma Mahamattas in his 14th regnal year to propagate Dhamma.
The Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra under Ashoka, presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa.
Kanishka started the Saka Era in 78 CE; the Fourth Buddhist Council was held at Kundalvana (Kashmir) during his reign.
Kanishka patronised Mahayana Buddhism; Gandhara art flourished under the Kushanas.
Ashvaghosha, court poet of Kanishka, wrote the Buddhacharita and Saundarananda.
Charaka, author of the Charaka Samhita on Ayurveda, was the court physician of Kanishka.
Sushruta, author of the Sushruta Samhita, is called the 'Father of Surgery' in India.
Nagarjuna propounded the Madhyamaka (Shunyavada) philosophy and is sometimes called the 'Indian Einstein'.
Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to assume the title Maharajadhiraja; the Gupta Era began in 319-320 CE.
Samudragupta is called the 'Napoleon of India' by V. A. Smith; his conquests are recorded on the Allahabad Pillar inscription by Harisena.
Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) made Ujjain his second capital; his court had the Navaratnas including Kalidasa and Varahamihira.
Fa-Hien, the Chinese traveller, visited India during Chandragupta II's reign and wrote 'Fo-Kuo-Ki'.
Aryabhata wrote the Aryabhatiya in 499 CE, explained eclipses and the earth's rotation, and worked with zero and place value.
Kalidasa's works include Abhijnana Shakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Malavikagnimitram and Vikramorvasiyam.
Varahamihira wrote the Brihat Samhita and the Pancha Siddhantika on astronomy and astrology.
Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by Kumaragupta I (Shakraditya) in the 5th century CE.
Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited India during Harshavardhana's reign, studied at Nalanda under Shilabhadra and wrote 'Si-Yu-Ki'.
Harshavardhana of the Pushyabhuti dynasty ruled from Kannauj and wrote the plays Ratnavali, Priyadarshika and Nagananda; Banabhatta wrote his biography Harshacharita.
Mahmud of Ghazni raided India 17 times between 1000 and 1027 CE, sacking the Somnath temple in 1025.
Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain (1191) but lost the Second Battle of Tarain (1192).
Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Slave dynasty, earned the title 'Lakh Baksh', and began the Qutub Minar; he built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra.
Iltutmish completed the Qutub Minar, introduced the silver tanka and copper jital, and organised the Chahalgani (group of forty nobles).
Razia Sultana (1236-1240) was the first and only woman to sit on the throne of Delhi.
Balban followed a 'Blood and Iron' policy, created the Diwan-i-Arz (military department), and introduced the court rituals Sijda and Paibos.
Alauddin Khalji introduced market control reforms, the land measurement system (Masahat), and the Dagh (branding of horses) and Chehra (descriptive rolls) systems.
Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced token currency, transferred the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad, and raised land revenue in the Doab.
Firoz Shah Tughlaq founded Jaunpur, Firozabad and Fatehabad, imposed Jizya on Brahmins, and built extensive canals.
Timur invaded India in 1398 during the reign of the Tughlaq ruler Nasiruddin Mahmud.
Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526, using gunpowder artillery organised by Rumi Khan.
Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama) in Turkish; it was translated into Persian by Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana.
Humayun was defeated by Sher Shah at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj/Bilgram (1540); his sister Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayunama.
Sher Shah Suri built the Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-i-Azam), introduced the silver rupiya coin, and systematised land measurement (zabt).
Akbar ascended the throne in 1556 at age 13 under Bairam Khan's regency and defeated Hemu at the Second Battle of Panipat.
Akbar founded Din-i-Ilahi in 1582, built the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri, abolished Jizya in 1564, and introduced the Mansabdari system.
Raja Todar Mal, Akbar's finance minister, introduced the Dahsala (Zabt) land revenue system.
Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari; Tansen (Mian Tansen) was the legendary musician of Akbar's court.
Shah Jahan, called the 'Prince of Builders', built the Taj Mahal, Red Fort and Jama Masjid; the Peacock Throne was made by Bebadal Khan.
Aurangzeb had the longest Mughal reign (1658-1707), reimposed Jizya in 1679, banned court music, and died at Ahmednagar.
Shivaji was crowned in 1674 at Raigad, ran administration through the Ashtapradhan council, and levied Chauth (one-fourth) and Sardeshmukhi (one-tenth).
The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between Robert Clive and Siraj-ud-daulah; Mir Jafar's betrayal decided it.
The Battle of Buxar (1764) was the decisive British victory that led to the grant of Diwani of Bengal through the Treaty of Allahabad (1765).
The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Marathas led by Sadashivrao Bhau.
Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773, under the Regulating Act) and founded the Calcutta Madrasa in 1781.
Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement of Bengal in 1793 and the Cornwallis Code of administrative reforms.
Tipu Sultan, the 'Tiger of Mysore', died fighting at Seringapatam in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799).
Lord Wellesley introduced the Subsidiary Alliance system in 1798; the Nizam of Hyderabad was the first to accept it.
Lord Dalhousie applied the Doctrine of Lapse from 1848, annexing Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur, and introduced railways, telegraph and a uniform postal system.
India's first railway ran from Bombay to Thane on 16 April 1853, covering 34 km.
The Revolt of 1857 began at Meerut on 10 May 1857; Mangal Pandey had revolted earlier at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857.
Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed emperor by the 1857 rebels and later exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1862.
Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi died fighting at Gwalior in June 1858; Tantia Tope was captured and hanged in 1859.
The Queen's Proclamation of 1 November 1858 at Allahabad ended East India Company rule and transferred power to the British Crown.
The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume; its first session at Bombay was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee with 72 delegates.
The Partition of Bengal (1905) by Lord Curzon sparked the Swadeshi Movement; the partition was annulled in 1911 and the capital shifted to Delhi.
The Surat Split of 1907 divided the Congress into Moderates and Extremists (Lal-Bal-Pal: Lajpat Rai, Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal).
The Lucknow Pact (1916) brought the Congress and Muslim League together; Tilak and Annie Besant led the Home Rule Movement the same year.
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 when General Dyer ordered firing at Amritsar; the Hunter Commission inquired into it.
The Rowlatt Act of 1919, called the 'Black Act', allowed detention without trial and triggered nationwide protest.
Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920 and withdrew it after the Chauri Chaura incident of 5 February 1922.
The all-white Simon Commission (1927) was boycotted across India; Lala Lajpat Rai died of injuries from a police lathi charge in 1928.
The Nehru Report (1928), drafted under Motilal Nehru, demanded dominion status for India.
At the Lahore session of 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the Congress adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution and fixed 26 January 1930 as Independence Day.
Gandhi's Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati to Dandi (240 miles); he broke the salt law on 6 April 1930.
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931, after which Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference in London.
The Poona Pact of 24 September 1932 between Gandhi and Ambedkar provided reserved seats for the depressed classes in place of separate electorates.
The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced provincial autonomy and a Federal Court; the Reserve Bank of India was established in 1935.
The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 with Gandhi's 'Do or Die' call; Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank, Bombay.
Subhas Chandra Bose revived the INA in 1943, gave the slogan 'Give me blood, I will give you freedom', and popularised 'Jai Hind'; he founded the Forward Bloc in 1939.
The Cabinet Mission (1946) had three members: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander.
The Mountbatten Plan of 3 June 1947 led to the Indian Independence Act and independence on 15 August 1947.
Lord Mountbatten was the first Governor-General of independent India; C. Rajagopalachari was the first Indian to hold the post (1948).
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel integrated the princely states and is called the 'Iron Man of India'; Hyderabad was integrated through Operation Polo (September 1948).
The Nizam of Hyderabad at accession was Mir Osman Ali Khan; Junagadh's Nawab fled to Pakistan and a 1948 plebiscite favoured India.
Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession of Jammu and Kashmir on 26 October 1947.
Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated on 30 January 1948 at Birla House, Delhi, by Nathuram Godse.
India's first general election was held in 1951-52; G. V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
Rajendra Prasad became India's first President in 1950 and Jawaharlal Nehru its first Prime Minister.
The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model; the Second Plan (1956-61) followed the Mahalanobis model.
M. S. Swaminathan is called the father of India's Green Revolution; Norman Borlaug was its global pioneer.
Verghese Kurien led the White Revolution through Operation Flood and the Amul cooperative movement.
Fourteen major banks were nationalised on 19 July 1969; six more were nationalised in 1980.
Bangladesh was liberated on 16 December 1971 (Victory Day); the Shimla Agreement followed in 1972.
The Emergency of 1975-77 was imposed under Article 352; the 42nd Amendment of 1976 is called the 'Mini Constitution'.
India's first nuclear test, 'Smiling Buddha', was conducted at Pokhran on 18 May 1974; Pokhran-II ('Operation Shakti') followed on 11 and 13 May 1998.
The Mandal Commission's recommendation of 27% OBC reservation was implemented by the V. P. Singh government in 1990.
The 1991 economic reforms (LPG: liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation) were steered by P. V. Narasimha Rao with Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister.
The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj, following the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957); Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated at Nagaur, Rajasthan, in 1959.
The Right to Information Act was passed in 2005.
MGNREGA (2005) guarantees 100 days of wage employment per rural household; it was renamed after Mahatma Gandhi in 2009.
The Goods and Services Tax was launched on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment with the slogan 'One Nation, One Tax'.
India lies between 8°4'N and 37°6'N latitude and 68°7'E and 97°25'E longitude.
The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
India's Standard Meridian is 82°30'E, passing through Mirzapur (Uttar Pradesh); IST is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT.
India's longest land border is with Bangladesh (4,096.7 km) and its shortest is with Afghanistan (106 km, Wakhan corridor).
The McMahon Line separates India and China in Arunachal Pradesh; the Radcliffe Line separates India and Pakistan; the Durand Line separates Pakistan and Afghanistan.
K2 (Godwin-Austen, 8,611 m) is India's highest peak, located in PoK; Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) is the highest peak within India's undisputed territory.
Nanda Devi (7,816 m) in Uttarakhand is the highest peak located entirely within India.
Anaimudi (2,695 m) in Kerala is the highest peak of peninsular India, in the Western Ghats.
Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills; Mahendragiri (1,501 m) is the highest of the Eastern Ghats.
The Aravalli range is India's oldest fold mountain range; its highest peak is Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) at Mount Abu.
The Vindhya and Satpura are block mountains; the Narmada flows westward in the rift valley between them.
The Narmada (1,312 km) is India's longest west-flowing river, rising at Amarkantak and forming the Dhuandhar Falls and Marble Rocks at Bhedaghat.
The Tapi (Tapti), rising at Multai in Betul (Madhya Pradesh), is the second-longest west-flowing peninsular river.
The Godavari (1,465 km), called Dakshin Ganga, is the longest peninsular river, rising at Trimbakeshwar near Nashik.
The Krishna (1,400 km) rises at Mahabaleshwar; the Kaveri rises at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri Hills and forms the Sivasamudram Falls.
The Mahanadi rises at Sihawa in Chhattisgarh; the Hirakud Dam built on it is among the longest dams in the world.
The Brahmaputra originates as the Yarlung Tsangpo at the Chemayungdung glacier in Tibet, enters India as the Siang/Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh, and is called Jamuna in Bangladesh.
The Indus originates near Lake Mansarovar; its Indian tributaries include the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.
The Ganga (2,525 km) begins as the Bhagirathi at the Gangotri glacier; at Devprayag the Alaknanda joins it to form the Ganga.
The Sundarbans, formed by the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta, is the world's largest delta and home to the Royal Bengal Tiger.
Chilika (Odisha) is India's largest brackish-water coastal lagoon; Wular (Jammu and Kashmir) is its largest freshwater lake.
Sambhar (Rajasthan) is India's largest inland salt lake; Vembanad (Kerala) is its longest lake.
Loktak (Manipur) is the largest freshwater lake of northeast India, known for floating phumdis and the Keibul Lamjao National Park.
The Thar Desert is called the Great Indian Desert; the Luni is its chief river, ending in the Rann of Kutch.
The Rann of Kutch is a vast salt marsh; the Little Rann hosts the Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary.
The Western Ghats, a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2012), are higher and more continuous than the Eastern Ghats; the Palghat Gap divides them.
The Deccan Traps' basaltic lava produced black regur soil, ideal for cotton; it was formed by volcanic eruptions about 66 million years ago.
Laterite soil, rich in iron and aluminium, forms by leaching in high-rainfall areas such as the Western Ghats.
Alluvial soil covers the largest area in India; khadar is new alluvium and bangar is old alluvium.
Red soil, coloured by iron oxide, is widespread in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
Mawsynram in Meghalaya is the wettest place on earth, receiving about 11,872 mm of rainfall annually.
Tamil Nadu gets most of its rain from the retreating (northeast) monsoon in October-November.
Western Disturbances from the Mediterranean bring winter rainfall to northwest India.
Mango Showers are pre-monsoon rains in Kerala and Karnataka; the Nor'wester (Kalbaisakhi) strikes West Bengal; the Loo is the hot dry wind of North India.
Karnataka is India's largest coffee producer; Assam is the largest tea producer and the Tea Board is headquartered at Kolkata.
Jute is called the Golden Fibre; West Bengal is the largest producer and India's first jute mill was set up at Rishra in 1855.
Uttar Pradesh is India's largest sugarcane producer; Brazil is the world's largest.
Gujarat and Maharashtra lead in cotton production; cotton is called 'white gold'.
Odisha has India's largest iron-ore reserves (Keonjhar); the Bailadila mines are in Chhattisgarh.
Jharkhand holds India's largest coal reserves; the first coal mine was opened at Raniganj in 1774 and Coal India is headquartered at Kolkata.
Odisha is India's largest bauxite producer; Koderma in Jharkhand is famous for mica.
The Suez Canal, connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea, opened in 1869 and was nationalised by Egypt's Nasser in 1956.
The Panama Canal, linking the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, opened in 1914.
The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert; the Antarctic Polar Desert is the largest desert overall.
The Nile (about 6,650 km) is the world's longest river; the Amazon carries the greatest volume of water.
Angel Falls in Venezuela is the world's highest waterfall.
The Constituent Assembly was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946; its first meeting was held on 9 December 1946 under Sachchidananda Sinha.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly; Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired its Drafting Committee.
The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.
The Drafting Committee had seven members with B. R. Ambedkar as chairman; it took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to complete the Constitution.
The Preamble begins with 'We the People of India' and secures Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity; the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity were added by the 42nd Amendment.
Fundamental Rights were borrowed from the USA, Directive Principles from Ireland, the federal structure with a strong centre from Canada, and parliamentary government from Britain.
Emergency provisions were borrowed from the Weimar Constitution of Germany and the Concurrent List from Australia.
Fundamental Rights are contained in Articles 12 to 35; originally seven, they are now six after the Right to Property was removed by the 44th Amendment.
The Right to Property is now only a legal right under Article 300A, not a Fundamental Right.
Article 14 guarantees equality before law, Article 15 prohibits discrimination, and Article 16 ensures equality of opportunity in public employment.
Article 17 abolishes untouchability, Article 19 guarantees six freedoms, and Article 21 protects life and personal liberty.
Article 32, the right to constitutional remedies, was called the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' by Ambedkar.
Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51) are non-justiciable; the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) upheld their harmony with Fundamental Rights.
Fundamental Duties under Article 51A were added by the 42nd Amendment; there are now 11 duties, the last added by the 86th Amendment on free education for ages 6-14.
The President (Article 52) is elected by an electoral college, holds office for five years, and must be at least 35 years old.
The President can be removed by impeachment under Article 61 on grounds of violation of the Constitution.
The Vice-President (Article 63) is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and is elected by members of both Houses of Parliament.
The Prime Minister is appointed by the President (Article 75) and the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
The Lok Sabha's maximum strength is 552; its normal term is five years unless dissolved earlier.
The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body with a maximum of 250 members, of whom one-third retire every two years.
A Money Bill (Article 110) can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and must be certified by the Speaker; the Rajya Sabha can only delay it by 14 days.
A no-confidence motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha and needs the support of at least 50 members to be admitted.
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha decides disqualification under the Tenth Schedule, subject to judicial review as held in Kihoto Hollohan (1992).
Parliament must meet at least twice a year with no more than six months between sessions; it normally has Budget, Monsoon and Winter sessions.
A joint sitting of Parliament (Article 118) is presided over by the Speaker and has been held only three times: 1961, 1978 and 2002.
The Supreme Court of India came into being on 28 January 1950; its first Chief Justice was Harilal J. Kania.
The basic structure doctrine, limiting Parliament's power to amend the Constitution, was laid down in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973).
The five writs under Articles 32 and 226 are Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto.
The Election Commission (Article 324) conducts elections; the first Chief Election Commissioner was Sukumar Sen.
Electronic Voting Machines were first used in India in the 1982 Parur by-election in Kerala.
The Comptroller and Auditor General (Article 148) audits government accounts; the first CAG was V. Narahari Rao.
The Attorney General of India (Article 76) is the government's chief legal adviser; the first was M. C. Setalvad.
The Finance Commission (Article 280) is constituted every five years; the first was chaired by K. C. Neogy and the 16th by Arvind Panagariya.
NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015; it is chaired by the Prime Minister.
The GST Council (Article 279A) is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and decides GST rates by consensus.
National Emergency (Article 352) has been proclaimed three times: 1962, 1971 and 1975; Financial Emergency (Article 360) has never been used.
The 42nd Amendment (1976) is called the Mini Constitution; many of its changes were rolled back by the 44th Amendment (1978).
The 73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj with a three-tier system and one-third reservation for women.
The 74th Amendment gave constitutional status to municipalities: Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council and Municipal Corporation.
Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language of the Union (Article 343); the Eighth Schedule now lists 22 languages.
The Constitution originally had 8 Schedules; there are now 12, including the anti-defection Tenth Schedule added by the 52nd Amendment (1985).
Citizenship provisions are in Articles 5 to 11; the Citizenship Act was passed in 1955 and amended by the CAA in 2019.
Article 370, giving special status to Jammu and Kashmir, was abrogated on 5-6 August 2019; Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh became Union Territories on 31 October 2019.
The new Parliament building was inaugurated on 28 May 2023.
The delimitation of constituencies is frozen until 2026 under the 84th Amendment.
NOTA (None of the Above) was introduced in Indian elections in 2013 following the PUCL judgment.
The Public Accounts Committee, established in 1921, has had its chairman from the opposition since 1967-68; the Estimates Committee is Parliament's largest with 30 members.
Zero Hour is an Indian parliamentary innovation beginning after Question Hour, with no mention in the rules of procedure.
Newton's three laws of motion and the law of gravitation were published in the Principia in 1687.
The speed of light in vacuum is 299,792,458 metres per second, about 3×10^8 m/s.
Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases; its speed in air is about 343 m/s and it cannot travel through vacuum.
Ultrasonic waves have frequencies above 20,000 Hz; bats navigate using them and SONAR uses them underwater.
Ohm's law states V = IR; the SI unit of electrical resistance is the ohm.
One horsepower equals 746 watts; the watt is the SI unit of power.
Alternating current was championed by Tesla and Westinghouse, while Edison backed direct current.
A transformer works on the principle of mutual induction and steps voltage up or down without changing frequency.
Fuse wire is made of a lead-tin alloy with a low melting point and high resistance.
A rainbow forms by dispersion and total internal reflection of sunlight in raindrops.
The sky appears blue due to Rayleigh scattering of shorter wavelengths by air molecules.
Optical fibres transmit light by total internal reflection and are used in endoscopy and communications.
LASER stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation; the first working laser was built by Theodore Maiman in 1960.
Nuclear fission was discovered by Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann in 1938 and explained by Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch.
Einstein's mass-energy equation is E = mc²; he won the Nobel Prize in 1921 for the photoelectric effect, not relativity.
Mendeleev published the periodic table in 1869 with 63 known elements; the modern table is ordered by atomic number following Moseley.
Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, oxygen in the earth's crust, and nitrogen (78%) in the atmosphere.
Diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon; diamond is the hardest natural substance while graphite conducts electricity.
The pH scale was introduced by Sørensen; human blood has a pH of about 7.4 and lemon juice about 2.
Common salt is sodium chloride (NaCl), baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3), washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, and caustic soda is sodium hydroxide.
Bleaching powder is calcium oxychloride (CaOCl2); Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate and gypsum is its dihydrate.
Rusting of iron forms hydrated ferric oxide and needs both oxygen and moisture; galvanisation with zinc prevents it.
Stainless steel is an alloy of iron, chromium and nickel; brass is copper plus zinc, while bronze is copper plus tin.
Argon is the most abundant noble gas in air (about 0.93%); helium is used in balloons and for deep-sea divers mixed with oxygen.
LPG is mainly propane and butane; the foul smell comes from added ethyl mercaptan, and CNG is mainly methane.
Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers; Avogadro's number is 6.022×10^23.
Radioactivity was discovered by Henri Becquerel in 1896; Marie Curie coined the term 'radioactivity'.
Robert Hooke discovered the cell in 1665 by observing cork; Schleiden and Schwann proposed the cell theory.
Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell, chloroplasts the kitchen, and lysosomes the suicidal bags.
Watson and Crick proposed the double-helix model of DNA in 1953, using Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data; they shared the 1962 Nobel Prize.
Photosynthesis converts carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen in the presence of chlorophyll and sunlight.
Karl Landsteiner discovered human blood groups and won the Nobel Prize in 1930; O negative is the universal donor and AB positive the universal recipient.
The normal human body temperature is 37°C (98.6°F) and normal blood pH is 7.4.
The femur is the longest bone and the stapes of the ear the smallest; the adult human body has 206 bones and over 600 muscles.
The skin is the largest organ of the body; the liver is the largest internal organ.
Insulin, discovered by Banting and Best in 1921, is secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas.
Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, B1 causes beriberi, C causes scurvy, D causes rickets, and K deficiency impairs blood clotting.
Iron deficiency causes anaemia, iodine deficiency causes goitre, and calcium deficiency leads to osteoporosis.
Mammalian red blood cells have no nucleus, live about 120 days, and carry oxygen through haemoglobin made in bone marrow.
White blood cells fight infection while platelets help blood clotting.
Malaria is caused by Plasmodium and spread by the female Anopheles mosquito; quinine, from cinchona bark, was the first cure.
Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 from the mould Penicillium notatum.
The modern Olympic Games began at Athens in 1896; the ancient games were held at Olympia from 776 BCE and the IOC was founded in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin.
The Olympic motto is 'Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter' (Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together); the IOC is headquartered at Lausanne, Switzerland.
Norman Pritchard won India's first Olympic medals, two silvers in athletics at Paris 1900.
India has won eight Olympic gold medals in men's hockey (1928-1980); Dhyan Chand, the 'Wizard of Hockey', was born on 29 August, observed as National Sports Day.
Neeraj Chopra won India's first Olympic athletics gold in javelin at Tokyo 2020 with a throw of 87.58 m and became world champion at Budapest 2023.
P. V. Sindhu won silver at Rio 2016 and bronze at Tokyo 2020, and became badminton world champion in 2019.
India won the Cricket World Cup in 1983 under Kapil Dev and in 2011 under M. S. Dhoni; the first World Cup in 1975 was won by the West Indies.
India won the 2024 T20 World Cup by beating South Africa by seven runs at Barbados, and the 2026 edition by beating New Zealand by 96 runs at Ahmedabad.
India won the 2025 Champions Trophy by beating New Zealand by four wickets at Dubai; Rohit Sharma was Player of the Match in the final and Rachin Ravindra Player of the Tournament.
Royal Challengers Bengaluru won their maiden IPL title in 2025, beating Punjab Kings by six runs at Ahmedabad under captain Rajat Patidar.
Mumbai Indians won their second Women's Premier League title in 2025, beating Delhi Capitals by eight runs at Brabourne Stadium; Harmanpreet Kaur was Player of the Match.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be hosted jointly by the USA, Canada and Mexico with 48 teams, the largest ever.
Viswanathan Anand is a five-time World Chess Champion (2000, 2007, 2008, 2010, 2012); D. Gukesh became the youngest world champion in 2024 at age 18.
Divya Deshmukh won the FIDE Women's World Cup 2025 at Batumi, beating Koneru Humpy in the final and earning the Grandmaster title.
India won its maiden Thomas Cup in badminton in 2022, beating Indonesia in the final at Bangkok.
The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna is India's highest sporting honour, followed by the Arjuna Award for sportspersons and the Dronacharya Award for coaches.
India finished fourth at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham with 61 medals including 22 gold; the 2026 Games will be held at Glasgow.
India won a record 107 medals including 28 gold at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou; the 2026 Asian Games will be held at Nagoya, Japan.
The Durand Cup, started in 1888, is Asia's oldest football tournament; the Rovers Cup (1891) is the second oldest.
Sunil Chhetri is India's all-time top football scorer and former captain, who reversed his 2024 retirement to return to the national team in 2025.
The Arthashastra on statecraft and economics was written by Kautilya (Chanakya), Chandragupta Maurya's minister.
Megasthenes, Seleucus Nicator's ambassador, wrote 'Indica' describing Mauryan India.
Kalhana's Rajatarangini is the historical chronicle of the kings of Kashmir.
Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita, a biography of Harshavardhana, and the novel Kadambari.
Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama and the Ain-i-Akbari chronicling Akbar's reign.
Babur wrote the Baburnama (Tuzuk-i-Baburi) in Turkish.
Rabindranath Tagore wrote Gitanjali, winning the Nobel Prize in 1913; he also wrote the national anthems of India (Jana Gana Mana) and Bangladesh (Amar Shonar Bangla).
Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote Anandamath, the source of the national song Vande Mataram.
Munshi Premchand wrote Godan, Nirmala and Gaban, and is called Upanyas Samrat.
Jawaharlal Nehru wrote The Discovery of India and Glimpses of World History while in prison.
Gandhi's autobiography is 'My Experiments with Truth'; his 1909 tract 'Hind Swaraj' outlines his political philosophy.
Dayananda Saraswati wrote Satyarth Prakash; Jyotiba Phule wrote Gulamgiri against caste oppression.
India is the world's largest producer of milk, pulses, jute and millets, and the second-largest producer of rice, wheat and sugarcane.
The first Indian to win the Nobel Prize was Rabindranath Tagore (Literature, 1913); the first Indian woman was Mother Teresa (Peace, 1979).
The first Indian Institute of Technology was set up at Kharagpur in 1951; the first Indian Institute of Management at Calcutta in 1961.
The first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal was Karnam Malleswari (weightlifting bronze, Sydney 2000).
The first Indian woman IPS officer was Kiran Bedi (1972 batch); the first woman Chief Minister was Sucheta Kripalani (Uttar Pradesh, 1963).
India's national animal is the Bengal tiger, national bird the peacock, national flower the lotus, and national tree the banyan.
Sarnath's Lion Capital is the national emblem; 'Satyameva Jayate' below it comes from the Mundaka Upanishad.
The national anthem Jana Gana Mana was adopted on 24 January 1950; it was first sung at the Calcutta Congress session in 1911.
The Dadasaheb Phalke Award, India's highest cinema honour, was first given to Devika Rani in 1969.
The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942 from Bombay's Gowalia Tank Maidan.
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar; General Dyer ordered the firing.
The Simon Commission arrived in India in 1928 and was boycotted with the slogan 'Simon Go Back'.
The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.
The Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, covering about 390 km.
The First Battle of Panipat (1526) was fought between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi.
The Second Battle of Panipat (1556) was fought between Akbar's forces and Hemu.
The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali.
The Battle of Plassey (1757) established British political supremacy in Bengal under Robert Clive.
The Battle of Buxar (1764) was won by the British under Hector Munro against Mir Qasim's alliance.
The Mughal emperor Akbar founded the Din-i-Ilahi in 1582.
Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in memory of Mumtaz Mahal; its chief architect is traditionally named as Ustad Ahmad Lahori.
The Qutub Minar was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish.
The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by Harihara and Bukka.
The Bhakti saint Kabir was a disciple of Ramananda.
Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi during Akbar's reign.
The Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875.
The Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828.
Swami Vivekananda addressed the Parliament of Religions at Chicago in 1893.
Annie Besant launched the Home Rule Movement in India in 1916.
The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume; its first session was at Bombay presided by W. C. Banerjee.
The Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dhaka.
The Lucknow Pact of 1916 brought the Congress and the Muslim League together.
The Rowlatt Act of 1919 allowed detention without trial and triggered nationwide protests.
The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919 introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
The Government of India Act 1935 introduced provincial autonomy and the federal scheme.
The Cabinet Mission arrived in India in 1946 to discuss transfer of power.
India became independent on 15 August 1947 and a republic on 26 January 1950.
The Preamble of the Indian Constitution declares India a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Constitution.
The Directive Principles of State Policy are in Part IV (Articles 36-51).
Article 370, granting special status to Jammu and Kashmir, was abrogated in August 2019.
The 42nd Amendment (1976) added the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble.
The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions.
The 86th Amendment (2002) made elementary education a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.
The President of India is elected by an electoral college of elected MPs and MLAs.
The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
The Lok Sabha has a maximum strength of 550 members under the Constitution.
The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house; one-third of its members retire every two years.
The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by the President under Article 148.
The Finance Commission is constituted every five years under Article 280.
The Election Commission is a three-member body headed by the Chief Election Commissioner.
The Supreme Court of India was established on 26 January 1950; its first Chief Justice was H. J. Kania.
A money bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the President's recommendation.
The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian states, including Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal.
The Standard Meridian of India (82°30'E) passes through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.
The Godavari (about 1,465 km) is the longest river flowing wholly within India; the Ganga flows on into Bangladesh.
The Brahmaputra is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet and the Jamuna in Bangladesh.
The Godavari is the longest peninsular river of India and is called the Dakshina Ganga.
The Narmada and Tapi are the major west-flowing rivers of peninsular India.
The Chilika Lake in Odisha is India's largest brackish-water lagoon.
The Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is one of India's largest freshwater lakes.
Nanda Devi (7,816 m) in Uttarakhand is the highest peak located entirely within India; Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) lies on the India–Nepal border.
The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site recognised in 2012.
The Thar Desert lies mainly in Rajasthan and is also called the Great Indian Desert.
India's longest coastline among states belongs to Gujarat.
Cherrapunji and Mawsynram in Meghalaya receive the world's highest rainfall.
The headquarters of the RBI is in Mumbai; it was established on 1 April 1935.
The RBI was nationalised in 1949.
Bank notes in India are issued by the RBI except the one-rupee note, issued by the Government of India.
The first Five-Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model.
NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.
GST was launched in India on 1 July 2017 as the 101st Constitutional Amendment.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was given statutory status in 1992.
The human body has 206 bones in an adult; babies are born with about 300.
The universal blood donor group is O negative and the universal recipient is AB positive.
Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy; Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets.
The pH of human blood is about 7.4, slightly alkaline.
The SI unit of force is the newton and of electrical resistance is the ohm.
The chemical formula of washing soda is Na2CO3·10H2O (sodium carbonate decahydrate); Na2CO3 alone is anhydrous soda ash. Baking soda is NaHCO3.
Diamond is the hardest natural substance; graphite is a soft allotrope of carbon.
The ozone layer, which absorbs ultraviolet radiation, lies in the stratosphere.
CNG (compressed natural gas) mainly consists of methane.
The first Indian to win a World Athletics Championships medal was Anju Bobby George (long jump bronze, Paris 2003).
Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold (10m air rifle, Beijing 2008).
P. V. Sindhu is the first Indian woman to win two Olympic medals.
The National Sports Day (29 August) marks the birth anniversary of Dhyan Chand.
Milkha Singh was known as the 'Flying Sikh'.
The first Commonwealth Games hosted by India were the 2010 Delhi Games.
The headquarters of the United Nations is in New York; it was founded in 1945.
The headquarters of UNESCO is in Paris and of WHO is in Geneva.
The International Court of Justice sits at The Hague in the Netherlands.
SAARC was founded in 1985 with its secretariat at Kathmandu.
The BRICS summit of 2024 was hosted by Russia at Kazan.
The G20 summit of 2023 was hosted by India in New Delhi.
The IMF and World Bank are together called the Bretton Woods twins.
The first Indian film, Raja Harishchandra (1913), was made by Dadasaheb Phalke.
The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest award in cinema.
The Jnanpith Award is India's highest literary honour.
Kalidasa wrote Abhijnanashakuntalam and Meghaduta in Sanskrit.
Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita, a biography of Harshavardhana.
Al-Biruni's 'Kitab-ul-Hind' describes India in the early 11th century.
The Ain-i-Akbari was written by Abul Fazl during Akbar's reign.
Babur wrote his memoirs, the Baburnama (Tuzk-e-Babri), in Chagatai Turkish.
Guru Nanak founded Sikhism in the 15th century; the Khalsa was founded by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699.
Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism, attained nirvana at Pawapuri in Bihar.
Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and gave his first sermon at Sarnath.
The Ajanta caves are famous for Buddhist murals and the Ellora caves for Hindu, Buddhist and Jain temples.
Hampi, the Vijayanagara capital, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Karnataka.
The Sun Temple at Konark was built by Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Jadeja's 16th first-class century (102 off 209) featured a 205-run fifth-wicket stand with Prerak Mankad (129) — Saurashtra 392 vs Chhattisgarh, Rajkot, 12 Oct 2026.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: CPI inflation: 5.54% in September 2026 (released 12 Oct, NSO provisional) vs 4.83% in August; food inflation 7.74%; RBI FY27 forecast raised to 5.2%.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Prerak Mankad top-scored with 129 off 150 balls (15 fours, one six) as Saurashtra posted 392 against Chhattisgarh at Rajkot on 12 Oct 2026.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Tushar Deshpande took a five-wicket haul including a hat-trick for Mumbai, reducing Chandigarh to 29-6 in Ranji Trophy 2026-27 round one (Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: Akshay Wadkar hit 198 and Yash Rathod 131 not out as Vidarbha posted 428 against Pondicherry in Ranji Trophy 2026-27 round one (Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: India's two-Test tour of New Zealand: 1st Test at Wellington, 19–23 Nov 2026; 2nd Test at Christchurch, 27 Nov–1 Dec 2026.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: The 92nd Ranji Trophy season began on 11 Oct 2026 — Saurashtra are in Elite Group B with Andhra, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Hyderabad, Karnataka, Punjab and Tripura.

oneliners.subject: Sports
oneliners.text: The Indian Olympic Association will elect its new Executive Council on 5 Dec 2026; Sanjay Kumar Srivastava was appointed returning officer on 10 Oct 2026.

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: Tamil Nadu CM Joseph Vijay met Andhra Pradesh CM N. Chandrababu Naidu in New Delhi on 13 Oct 2026, seeking additional drinking water for Chennai through the Telugu Ganga project (Krishna water).

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: Maharashtra drought relief: examination fees waived for 82,074 Class XI and XII students in Latur district (announced 13 Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: Tamil Nadu released a revised school timetable on 13 Oct 2026 providing physical education and co-curricular activities five days a week.

oneliners.subject: Current affairs
oneliners.text: India hosted its first BIMSTEC Home Ministers' meeting in New Delhi under Home Minister Amit Shah (13 Oct 2026).

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: NPCI will levy UPI Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on select Person-to-Merchant transactions after Diwali 2026.

oneliners.subject: Governance
oneliners.text: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PMDDKY) completed its first year on 11 October 2026.

oneliners.subject: Economy
oneliners.text: India’s trade deficit with China crossed $100 billion in 2026; exports to China grew 40% in the first three quarters to $20 billion (Oct 2026).
